# MethodCache: instructions for coding agents

Copy this file into your project as agent instructions, for example as `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, a Cursor
rule, a Claude Code skill or a section of `AGENTS.md`. It tells a coding agent how to add caching with MethodCache
correctly. Full docs: https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/README.md. The `MethodCache` package
carries the same docs in its `docs` folder (`~/.nuget/packages/methodcache/<version>/docs/`): `how-to.md` answers
common questions and `reference/` has the exact rules.

## Adding caching to a service

1. The `MethodCache` package contains the library, the source generator and the analyzers. Nothing else is needed
   for in-memory caching. All packages target .NET 10; install add-ons at the same version as `MethodCache`.
2. Put `[Cache]` on the **interface** method, never on the class. Put `[CacheInvalidate(Tags = [...])]` on the
   interface methods that change the data. Don't change the implementation.
3. Register services as usual, then call `builder.Services.AddMethodCache()` **after** them. Later cacheable
   registrations fail at host startup. A cached interface without a registration needs
   `AutoRegister(lifetime)` and exactly one class that implements it.
4. Use `MethodCacheBuilder` for startup, in one `AddMethodCache(mc => mc...)` call: `Defaults`, `Group`, typed
   `Method`, `Memory`, `Distributed`, `Telemetry`, `FromConfiguration`, `FromAssemblyOf<T>()` and the integrations'
   `UseRedis` / `UseSqlServer` / `UsePostgreSql` (one of them) / `UseMessagePack`. Don't use `services.Configure<...>` for MethodCache
   options.

```cs
using MethodCache;

public interface IProductService
{
    [Cache(Duration = "00:10:00", Tags = ["products", "product:{id}"])]
    Task<Product> GetAsync(int id, CancellationToken ct = default);

    [Cache(Duration = "00:01:00", Tags = ["products"])]
    Task<List<Product>> SearchAsync(string text, int page);

    [CacheInvalidate(Tags = ["products", "product:{id}"])]
    Task UpdateAsync(int id, Product product);
}

public sealed class ProductService(Database db) : IProductService
{
    public Task<Product> GetAsync(int id, CancellationToken ct = default) => db.LoadProductAsync(id, ct);

    public Task<List<Product>> SearchAsync(string text, int page) => db.SearchAsync(text, page);

    public Task UpdateAsync(int id, Product product) => db.SaveAsync(product);
}
```

```cs
builder.Services.AddSingleton<Database>();
builder.Services.AddScoped<IProductService, ProductService>();   // any lifetime
builder.Services.AddMethodCache();                               // after your registrations
```

## Rules

- Only interface methods that return a value can be cached: sync, `Task<T>` or `ValueTask<T>`. Return a list, never
  a lazy `IEnumerable<T>` or `IQueryable<T>`.
- Callers must use the interface. Calling the method from inside the class, or resolving the class itself, bypasses
  the cache.
- Keys are generated from the method and its arguments; don't write keys for `[Cache]` methods. A `CancellationToken`
  is not part of the key. Every value that changes the result must be a parameter.
- Tags take templates with a **parameter name** only: `"product:{id}"`. `"{product.Id}"` is not a template, stays
  literal and gives warning MC0016; add an `id` parameter instead. Use the same tags on the cached method and on its `[CacheInvalidate]`.
- Tag values are formatted like `MethodCacheKeys.Part`: `:` and `\` in strings are escaped, a `Guid` is written
  without hyphens, an enum as its number, `bool` as `true`/`false`, numbers and dates in the invariant culture. Prefer
  ids (`int`, `Guid`) and never pass passwords or tokens as arguments of cached methods.
- `[CacheInvalidate]` runs after the method, or its task, succeeds; never when it throws.
- Synchronous `[Cache]` methods use the memory cache only, also with Redis, SQL Server or PostgreSQL. Make a method
  async to share its results between instances.
- Durations accept invariant `[d.]hh:mm:ss` or unit strings such as `30s` and `1.5h`. Other settings: `SlidingExpiration` (or `"off"`), `RefreshAhead`
  (shorter than `Duration` and `SlidingExpiration`, or `"off"`; MC0023 otherwise), `FailSafe` (or `"off"`), `FailSafeTimeout`, `FailSafeRetryAfter`,
  `Version`, `Tags`, `Enabled`, `Distributed` and the named `Group` setting. In code each has one builder method with
  the same name: `WithFailSafe(d)`, `WithFailSafeTimeout(t)`, `WithFailSafeRetryAfter(t)` and so on.
- Cached objects are shared between callers: return immutable types such as records. Never cache `JsonNode`,
  `JsonObject`, `DataTable` or a `Stream` (MC0025); return a record, a string or a `JsonElement`.
- The key holds only the method's arguments. A cached implementation must not read the current user or request
  (`IHttpContextAccessor`, `ClaimsPrincipal`, row-level security on the connection; MC0026): pass the user or tenant id
  as an argument instead.
- Invalidate after a transaction commits, with `CancellationToken.None`, never before or inside it.
- For a type with only private state used as an argument or inside one (a property, a list element), implement
  `ICacheKeyProvider`.
- For library modules and Native AOT, select the containing assembly with `MethodCacheBuilder.FromAssemblyOf<T>()`.
  If multiple modules generate the same interface, the selected one wins; the other modules' services stay cached, and
  calling/entry assemblies have no special priority.
- In `appsettings.json`, the `MethodCache` section holds `Defaults`, `FailSafe`, `Groups` (by group name) and
  `Methods` (by method id, such as `[MyApp]MyApp.IProductService.GetAsync`; not `Services`). Write durations as
  `"00:05:00"` (a bare number is rejected), `Tags` as a list, and only known setting names. Anything else, an
  unknown method id and a method listed twice fail startup.
- `CacheWhen` is set for one method in code (`mc.Method(...).CacheWhen(...)`); in `Defaults` or a group it fails
  startup, and so does a `CacheWhen<T>` for a type the method can't return.
- A `Duration` may be at most `MethodCacheMemoryOptions.MaxExpiration` (7 days by default, at most 365); a longer one
  fails startup. Raise it with `mc.Memory(o => o.MaxExpiration = ...)`.
- For a client from a NuGet package with an interface, use
  `[assembly: CacheInterface(typeof(IClient), nameof(IClient.Method), Duration = "...")]` instead of a wrapper.
- Without an attribute, use `ICacheManager.GetOrCreateAsync(key, factory, o => o.WithDuration(...))` with an explicit,
  prefixed key such as `$"order:{id}"`.
- Fix MethodCache's `MC` build diagnostics; each links to its explanation, and many have a code fix.
- In tests, register `NoOpCacheManager` (namespace `MethodCache`) after `AddMethodCache()` to turn method caching
  off. When a test writes to the database directly, call `ICacheAdministrator.ClearAsync()` after the write.
- To invalidate a `GetOrCreateAsync` entry that has a version, pass the key and the version:
  `InvalidateKeyAsync(key, 2)`. Never pass a stored key (`MethodCacheKeys.StoredKey`) to `ICacheManager`.
- To invalidate one call of a `[Cache]` method, get its key from `IMethodCacheKeys`:
  `cache.InvalidateKeyAsync(keys.For<IProductService>(s => s.GetAsync(42)))`. For every entry of one method, use
  `ICacheAdministrator.InvalidateMethodAsync(keys.MethodId<IProductService>(s => s.GetAsync(0)))`.
- When data changes outside the cached interface (an endpoint or command writing to the database, or after a
  transaction commits), invalidate after the write with a tag from `IMethodCacheKeys.Tag`:
  `cache.InvalidateTagAsync(keys.Tag<IPriceSource>(s => s.GetRateAsync(provider, model), IPriceSource.RateTag))`.
  Never build a tag with string interpolation (`$"price:{model}"`): tags escape `:` and `\` in strings and write a
  `Guid` without hyphens and an enum as its number, so a hand-built tag can silently match nothing (MC0024).
- With Entity Framework Core, add package `MethodCache.EntityFrameworkCore` and map each entity type to the tags of
  the cached methods that read it: `mc.UseEntityFrameworkCore<AppDb>(ef => ef.Entity<Product>("product:{Id}", "products"))`.
  A name in braces is an entity property. `SaveChanges` then invalidates them after the commit, and a rollback drops
  them, also for rows updated or deleted without loading them, `OwnsOne`/`OwnsMany` types and many-to-many links;
  don't add invalidation code to those writes. For `ExecuteUpdate`, `ExecuteDelete` and `ExecuteSql…` (MC0027),
  call `db.InvalidateAfterCommit(tag)` inside the transaction, or `cache.InvalidateTagAsync(tag)` after a write
  without one.
- Several registrations of one interface with different implementation types each cache their own results.
- For a distributed cache use `UseRedis`, `UseSqlServer` or `UsePostgreSql`; MethodCache never uses the app's
  `IDistributedCache`. Values are JSON; use `UseJson(context)` for Native AOT and `UseJson(options)` for your own
  settings. A result type that doesn't read back unchanged (private setters, a derived type) stays in memory, with a
  warning: return records with public properties.
- `AddHttpCaching()` needs `AddMethodCache()` in the same container, in either order. It turns off automatic cookies;
  send cookies as a `Cookie` header, or set `KeepCookies = true`, which turns response caching off.
- Generated keys and method ids start with the service assembly's name in brackets. Never write a key or method id by
  hand: get keys from `IMethodCacheKeys.For`, tags from `IMethodCacheKeys.Tag` and ids from `IMethodCacheKeys.MethodId`.
- Telemetry: `MethodCacheTelemetryOptions` (`mc.Telemetry(...)`) records keys and tags on spans only when you turn it
  on, hashed by default. `AddMethodCacheInstrumentation()` (package `MethodCache.OpenTelemetry`) subscribes
  OpenTelemetry to the `MethodCache` meter and activity source.

## Namespaces

- `MethodCache`: `[Cache]`, `[CacheInvalidate]`, `[CacheInterface]`, `ICacheManager`, `ICacheAdministrator`,
  `IRuntimeCacheConfigurator`, `IMethodCacheKeys`, `MethodCacheKeys`, `MethodCacheMemoryOptions`, `Any<T>`,
  `ICacheKeyProvider`.
- `MethodCache`: also `NoOpCacheManager` (sealed).
- `Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection`: `AddMethodCache`. Everything else is a method on its builder:
  `FromConfiguration`, `Distributed(...)`, `Telemetry(...)`, `UseRedis` (package `MethodCache.Redis`), `UseSqlServer`
  (package `MethodCache.SqlServer`), `UsePostgreSql` (package `MethodCache.PostgreSql`), `UseMessagePack` (package `MethodCache.Serialization.MessagePack`)
  and `UseEntityFrameworkCore<TContext>` (package `MethodCache.EntityFrameworkCore`).
- `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore`: `InvalidateAfterCommit` on a `DbContext` (package `MethodCache.EntityFrameworkCore`).

<!-- source: docs/getting-started.md -->

# Getting started

MethodCache 1.0 is a release candidate on nuget.org, so add `--prerelease` until 1.0.0 is out (the same goes for
the add-on packages):

```bash
dotnet add package MethodCache --prerelease
```

The `MethodCache` package contains the library, the source generator and the analyzers. It requires .NET 10 and the
.NET 10 SDK, as every add-on package does.

## 1. Start from a service

A typical service talks to a database on every call:

```cs
public sealed class ProductService(Database db)
{
    public Task<Product> GetAsync(int id, CancellationToken ct = default) => db.LoadProductAsync(id, ct);

    public Task<List<Product>> SearchAsync(string text, int page) => db.SearchAsync(text, page);

    public Task UpdateAsync(int id, Product product) => db.SaveAsync(product);
}
```

## 2. Put the attributes on its interface

`[Cache]` goes on interface methods that return data, `[CacheInvalidate]` on the methods that change it. The class
only gains `: IProductService`; its methods don't change:

```cs
using MethodCache;

public interface IProductService
{
    [Cache(Duration = "00:10:00", Tags = ["products", "product:{id}"])]
    Task<Product> GetAsync(int id, CancellationToken ct = default);

    [Cache(Duration = "00:01:00", Tags = ["products"])]
    Task<List<Product>> SearchAsync(string text, int page);

    [CacheInvalidate(Tags = ["products", "product:{id}"])]
    Task UpdateAsync(int id, Product product);
}

public sealed class ProductService(Database db) : IProductService
{
    public Task<Product> GetAsync(int id, CancellationToken ct = default) => db.LoadProductAsync(id, ct);

    public Task<List<Product>> SearchAsync(string text, int page) => db.SearchAsync(text, page);

    public Task UpdateAsync(int id, Product product) => db.SaveAsync(product);
}
```

- `GetAsync(42)` is stored for ten minutes under a key built from the method and its argument
  (`...IProductService.GetAsync:42`). The `CancellationToken` is not part of the key.
- `"product:{id}"` is a tag template: `GetAsync(42)` is tagged `product:42`.
- `UpdateAsync(42, ...)` removes every entry tagged `products` or `product:42` once it has completed.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The attributes must be on the interface. On a class they do nothing, and the analyzer reports
> [MC0001](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mc0001) with a code fix that moves them.

## 3. Register it

```cs
builder.Services.AddSingleton<Database>();
builder.Services.AddScoped<IProductService, ProductService>();   // any lifetime
builder.Services.AddMethodCache();                               // after your registrations
```

`AddMethodCache()` wraps every registered interface that has cached methods in its generated decorator and keeps the
lifetime you chose. Register your cached services before it: a cached service registered after it fails at startup
with an error that says so.

- Keyed registrations (`AddKeyedScoped<IProductService, ProductService>("primary")`) are cached too, each with its own
  entries.
- Several registrations of one interface with different classes, resolved as `IEnumerable<IProductService>`, each cache
  their own results.
- Generic interfaces such as `IRepository<User>` are cached for each closed type a class implements.
- A service you haven't registered is registered only when you ask: `AddMethodCache(mc => mc.AutoRegister(ServiceLifetime.Scoped))`.

[Registration](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/reference/registration.md) has the exact rules, including open generic registrations and several
assemblies that generate the same interface.

### Registering with a factory

A factory registration is cached like any other: register it before `AddMethodCache()`, and the decorator wraps
what your factory returns, with the lifetime you chose.

```cs
builder.Services.AddScoped<IProductService>(
    sp => new ProductService(sp.GetRequiredService<Database>()));
builder.Services.AddMethodCache();
```

## What can be cached

```cs
[Cache] Product Get(int id);                          // synchronous
[Cache] Task<Product> GetAsync(int id);               // Task<T>
[Cache] ValueTask<Product> GetFastAsync(int id);      // ValueTask<T>
[Cache] Task<Product?> FindAsync(string name);        // null results are cached too
```

- Synchronous methods, `Task<T>` and `ValueTask<T>` can be cached. A method that returns nothing has nothing to
  cache, so `[Cache]` on it is a build error ([MC0003](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mc0003),
  [MC0022](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mc0022)). So is a lazy `IEnumerable<T>` or `IQueryable<T>`
  ([MC0015](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mc0015)): return a list.
- Synchronous methods use the memory cache only, also with a distributed cache configured
  ([Generated decorators](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/source-generator.md#synchronous-methods)).
- Exceptions are never cached: the next call runs the method again.
- Concurrent calls with the same arguments share one call to your method (stampede protection). A caller that cancels
  only stops its own wait.
- Without a `Duration`, entries live five minutes (the built-in default) unless you set a
  default ([Expiration](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/expiration.md#duration)).
- `null` results are cached. To skip null for one method, give it a
  [condition](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/conditional-caching.md) (`CacheWhen(x => x is not null)`); `CacheNullValues = false` on the
  [memory cache](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/memory-cache.md) turns it off for every method.
- The cached object is returned as is, not copied. Treat cached results as read-only.

## Per-user data

A cached result is shared by every caller with the same arguments. The key is built from the arguments only, so
anything else the result depends on must be an argument too:

- **The signed-in user or tenant.** Pass the id: `GetOrdersAsync(int userId)`, not a method that reads the user from
  `IHttpContextAccessor` or a `ClaimsPrincipal`. MethodCache warns about a cached implementation that takes those
  (MC0026).
- **Row-level security.** When the database filters rows by a setting on the connection, such as the current user,
  the same call returns different rows for different users. Make that setting an argument of the cached method, or
  don't cache the method.
- **Scoped services.** A scoped `DbContext` works as usual for a normal call. A refresh-ahead or fail-safe load can
  outlive the request, so it runs on a new instance from a new DI scope, with no `HttpContext`
  ([Refresh-ahead](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/expiration.md#refresh-ahead)). A service that sets up its connection per request must do
  the same from the method's arguments.

## Next steps

- Choose how long entries live: [Expiration](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/expiration.md).
- Remove entries when data changes: [Invalidation](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/invalidation.md).
- Change durations without a redeploy: [Configuration](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/configuration.md).
- Share the cache between instances: [Distributed cache](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/distributed-cache.md).
- Look up a task or a question: [How do I…?](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/how-to.md).

# How do I…?

Short answers to common questions, each with a link to the page that has the details. Search this page for a word
from your question.

## Getting started

**Why does MethodCache need an interface?**
The source generator writes a class that implements your interface, checks the cache and calls your implementation
on a miss. Dependency injection hands out that class in place of yours. A class without an interface can't be
replaced that way: add an interface, or use [manual caching](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/manual-caching.md) with `ICacheManager`.
([Getting started](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md))

**Can I put `[Cache]` on the class instead?**
No. Put it on the interface method. On a class member it does nothing, and warning MC0001 says so; its code fix moves
the attribute to the interface. ([Build diagnostics](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md))

**Where do I call `AddMethodCache()`?**
After you register the services it caches. A cached service registered after it fails when the host starts.
([Registration reference](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/reference/registration.md#order))

**Why does my method still run on every call?**
The caller uses the class instead of the interface, the call comes from inside the class, or the service was
registered after `AddMethodCache()`. ([Troubleshooting](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md#the-method-runs-on-every-call))

**Which return types can be cached?**
Synchronous values, `Task<T>` and `ValueTask<T>`. Return a list, never a lazy `IEnumerable<T>` or `IQueryable<T>`.
([Generated decorators](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/source-generator.md))

**Are synchronous methods cached in Redis, SQL Server or PostgreSQL?**
No, synchronous methods use the memory cache only, so they never block on the network. Make the method async to share
its results between instances. ([Distributed cache reference](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/reference/distributed.md#which-calls-use-the-distributed-cache))

## Invalidation

**When does `[CacheInvalidate]` run?**
After the method, or the task it returns, succeeds. When it throws, nothing is invalidated.
([Invalidation](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/invalidation.md))

**The data changes somewhere else (an endpoint, a repository, a message handler). How do I invalidate?**
After the write, call `ICacheManager.InvalidateTagAsync` with a tag from `IMethodCacheKeys.Tag`, which formats it
exactly as the cached method does:
`await cache.InvalidateTagAsync(keys.Tag<IPriceSource>(s => s.GetRateAsync(provider, model), "price:{provider}:{model}"))`.
([When the write happens somewhere else](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/invalidation.md#when-the-write-happens-somewhere-else))

**How do I invalidate after a database transaction commits?**
With Entity Framework Core, `MethodCache.EntityFrameworkCore` does it: tags mapped to an entity type are invalidated
after the commit, and dropped on a rollback. A transaction passed in with `UseTransaction` is invalidated when a
connected context commits it, or when it is over. ([Entity Framework Core](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/entity-framework-core.md#when-the-tags-are-invalidated))
Otherwise invalidate after `CommitAsync` returns, not inside the transaction, and pass `CancellationToken.None`: a
reader between the invalidation and the commit would cache the old data again.
([After a database transaction](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/invalidation.md#after-a-database-transaction))

**How do I make sure no write path forgets to invalidate?**
With Entity Framework Core, map each entity to its tags with `mc.UseEntityFrameworkCore<AppDb>(ef => ef.Entity<Product>("product:{Id}"))`:
every `SaveChanges` that changes one invalidates them, wherever it runs. Otherwise send every write through an
interface whose methods commit their own transaction and carry `[CacheInvalidate]`. Test each write path with a cached
read before and after it. ([Entity Framework Core](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/entity-framework-core.md#mapping-entities-to-tags))

**My endpoint writes with `ExecuteUpdateAsync`. Why the warning MC0027?**
It changes rows without EF Core's change tracker, so no entity tags are known for them. Inside a transaction, add
`db.InvalidateAfterCommit(tag)`; without one, call `ICacheManager.InvalidateTagAsync` after the write.
([Writes the change tracker doesn't see](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/entity-framework-core.md#writes-the-change-tracker-doesnt-see))

**Does the Entity Framework Core package work with Cosmos DB or MongoDB?**
Yes, entity tags and `InvalidateAfterCommit` act on `SaveChanges`. A MongoDB transaction you begin yourself is
invalidated at the context's next save or when it is disposed. ([Document databases](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/entity-framework-core.md#document-databases))

**I update a row from a request without loading it. Is the old category still invalidated?**
Yes. A row saved with `Update`, `Attach` or `Remove(new Product { Id = id })` is read once before the save, so the
tags of its stored values are invalidated too. ([Mapping entities to tags](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/entity-framework-core.md#mapping-entities-to-tags))

**Can I build a tag string myself, such as `$"price:{model}"`?**
Only with `MethodCacheKeys.Part` around each value. MethodCache writes a `Guid` without hyphens (format `N`), an enum
as its number, `bool` as `true`/`false`, numbers and dates in the invariant culture, and escapes `:` and `\` in strings,
so `gemma3:4b` becomes `gemma3\:4b`. A tag formatted differently matches nothing, silently. Analyzer MC0024 warns
about hand-built tags and its code fix adds `MethodCacheKeys.Part`. ([Build diagnostics](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md))

**How do I invalidate one call of a cached method?**
`await cache.InvalidateKeyAsync(keys.For<IProductService>(s => s.GetAsync(42)))`.
([Invalidation](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/invalidation.md#from-code))

**How do I invalidate every entry of one method?**
`await admin.InvalidateMethodAsync(keys.MethodId<IProductService>(s => s.GetAsync(0)))` with `ICacheAdministrator`.
([Invalidation](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/invalidation.md#from-code))

**How do I invalidate everything for a tenant or a user?**
Add a tag such as `"tenant:{tenantId}"` to every method that returns that tenant's data, and invalidate that tag.
([Tag templates](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/invalidation.md#tag-templates))

**Does an invalidation reach my other instances?**
Yes, with Redis, SQL Server or PostgreSQL configured. Other instances drop their copy when the message arrives: at once
with Redis and PostgreSQL, on the next poll (one second) with SQL Server.
([With several instances](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/invalidation.md#with-several-instances))

**How do I pass a version and a cancellation token?**
`InvalidateKeyAsync(key, ct)`, `InvalidateKeyAsync(key, 2, ct)`, `TryGetAsync<Order>(key, ct)` and
`TryGetAsync<Order>(key, 2, ct)`: the token always comes last. ([Manual caching](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/manual-caching.md))

## Expiration and what gets cached

**How do I set how long a result is cached?**
`[Cache(Duration = "00:10:00")]`, or `"30s"`, `"5m"`, `"1.5h"`, `"7d"`. Change it without a rebuild in
`appsettings.json`. ([Writing a duration](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/expiration.md#writing-a-duration),
[Configuration](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/configuration.md#appsettingsjson))

**How do I refresh a value before it expires?**
`RefreshAhead`, shorter than `Duration`: a call near the end of the duration returns the cached value and refreshes it
in the background. ([Refresh-ahead](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/expiration.md#refresh-ahead))

**How do I keep serving the last value when the database is down?**
`FailSafe`: when the method throws or is slower than `FailSafeTimeout`, the last good value is returned.
([Fail-safe](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/fail-safe.md))

**Is `null` cached?**
Yes, by default. `CacheNullValues = false` in `mc.Memory(...)` turns that off for every method. For one method, use
`CacheWhen`: `mc.Method((IProductService s) => s.FindAsync(Any<int>.Value)).CacheWhen(product => product is not null)`.
([Null values](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/memory-cache.md#null-values), [CacheWhen](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/conditional-caching.md#cachewhen))

**How do I cache only some results?**
`CacheWhen` decides per method from the result whether to store it. ([Conditional caching](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/conditional-caching.md))

**How do I skip the cache for one call?**
With manual caching, `WithEnabled(false)` for that call. For a `[Cache]` method, add a second interface method without
`[Cache]` that reads the source directly. ([Skipping the cache for one call](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/conditional-caching.md#skipping-the-cache-for-one-call))

**How do I turn caching off for a method without a rebuild?**
`"Enabled": false` for that method in `appsettings.json`, or `IRuntimeCacheConfigurator` at runtime.
([Configuration](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/configuration.md))

**What does the `Weigher` look like?**
`Func<string, object?, long>`: `(key, value) => weight`, called once when an entry is stored. Set it with
`WeightLimit` to bound the memory cache by size. ([Bounding by size](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/memory-cache.md#bounding-by-size))

**Can callers change a cached object?**
They share the same instance, so a change is seen by every caller. Return immutable types such as records.
([Cached objects are shared](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/memory-cache.md#cached-objects-are-shared))

**Can I cache a `JsonObject`, a `DataTable` or a `Stream`?**
No: every caller gets the same instance at once, and these change while they are read (a `JsonNode` parses lazily
and isn't thread-safe). Warning MC0025 says so. Return a record, a string or a `JsonElement`.
([MC0025](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mc0025))

**My service reads the current user from `HttpContext`. Can I cache it?**
Not as it is: the key holds only the method's arguments, so one user's result reaches the next. Pass the user or
tenant id as an argument. Warning MC0026 reports such services. The same goes for row-level security on the
connection. ([Per-user data](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md#per-user-data))

## Keys

**How are keys built?**
From the assembly, interface, method and the arguments' values. A `CancellationToken` is not part of the key.
([Cache keys](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/keys.md))

**My argument is a class with private fields. What happens?**
Arguments whose only state is private are rejected; implement `ICacheKeyProvider` on the type.
([Types whose state is private](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/keys.md#types-whose-state-is-private))

**How do I cache something without an attribute?**
`ICacheManager.GetOrCreateAsync(key, factory, o => o.WithDuration(...))` with a prefixed key such as `$"order:{id}"`.
([Manual caching](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/manual-caching.md))

**How do I cache a client from a NuGet package?**
`[assembly: CacheInterface(typeof(IClient), nameof(IClient.Method), Duration = "...")]` caches chosen methods of its
own interface. ([Caching third-party code](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/third-party.md))

## Running in production

**How do I share the cache between instances?**
`AddMethodCache(mc => mc.UseRedis("..."))`, `mc.UseSqlServer(...)` or `mc.UsePostgreSql(...)`.
([Distributed cache](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/distributed-cache.md))

**A result type stays in memory only, with a warning. Why?**
It doesn't read back from JSON unchanged: private setters, a derived type returned as its base type, or `object`.
Return records with public properties, or register a serializer with `UseJson(options)`.
([Serialization](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/distributed-cache.md#serialization))

**Can a worker process invalidate the API's memory cache without sharing values?**
Yes: `UsePostgreSql` (or Redis, SQL Server) with `Defaults(o => o.WithDistributed(false))`. Values stay in each
process's memory, and invalidations reach every process. ([Invalidations only](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/distributed-cache.md#invalidations-only))

**What happens when Redis is down?**
Calls keep working from memory and your methods. Each call waits at most one second, Redis is skipped for ten seconds
after a failure, and invalidations are retried. ([Distributed cache](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/distributed-cache.md))

**How do I see what's cached?**
`ICacheAdministrator`: `GetStatsAsync`, `GetMethods`, `ListEntries`. The admin endpoints in `MethodCache.AspNetCore`
show the same. ([Monitoring](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/monitoring.md))

**Why does `POST clear` need a `{}` body?**
The admin `POST` endpoints take only JSON, so a page on another site can't make a signed-in admin's browser call
them. Send `-H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "{}"`.
([ASP.NET Core](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/src/MethodCache.AspNetCore/README.md#endpoints))

**How do I get metrics into Prometheus?**
Use OpenTelemetry's Prometheus exporter with `AddMethodCacheInstrumentation()` on the meter builder. The meter is named
`MethodCache`, so `dotnet-counters monitor --counters MethodCache` shows it too.
([Monitoring](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/monitoring.md#standard-net-listeners))

**How do I publish with Native AOT?**
Register your `JsonSerializerContext` with `mc.UseJson(AppJsonContext.Default)`. ([Native AOT](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/native-aot.md))

## Testing

**How do I turn caching off in tests?**
Register `NoOpCacheManager` after `AddMethodCache()`. ([Testing](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/testing.md#turning-method-caching-off))

**A test writes to the database directly. How do I keep the cache from serving old data?**
Call `ICacheAdministrator.ClearAsync()` after the write, or invalidate the affected tag with `IMethodCacheKeys.Tag`.
([Testing](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/testing.md#when-a-test-writes-to-the-database-directly))

**How do I test expiration without waiting?**
Register a fake `TimeProvider`. ([Testing](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/testing.md#time))

## Coding agents

**How do I have an agent add MethodCache to my project?**
Give it the prompt in the README's [Using a coding agent](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/README.md#using-a-coding-agent). The `MethodCache` package
carries these docs in its `docs` folder, and [agent instructions](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/ai/methodcache.md) has the rules to copy into your
agent's instructions.


---

<!-- source: docs/features/source-generator.md -->

# Generated decorators

Put cache attributes on interface methods. The generator builds a decorator around the registered implementation
and routes cached calls through MethodCache. Your implementation stays ordinary application code.

The generator supports synchronous result methods, `Task<T>` and `ValueTask<T>`, overloaded methods, generic
interfaces and generic methods, including interfaces nested in generic containing types. Constraints on both
the containing type and the interface, including `unmanaged` and base class constraints, are preserved, and so are
`scoped` parameters on forwarded members. Each overload has its own
[method id](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/configuration.md#appsettingsjson) and its own cache entries.

Public interface members are forwarded to the implementation: uncached methods, properties, indexers and events.
Non-public and sealed default interface methods stay on the interface with their own bodies; the decorator doesn't
implement them, so `[Cache]` or `[CacheInvalidate]` on one (or on a `static` member) is warning
[MC0018](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mc0018). An interface with non-public abstract members is rejected with
[MC0014](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mc0014), because the decorator can't call those members on the implementation.

Keywords and unusual names are escaped, and your own types named like framework types (such as `Task` or `List`)
don't clash with the generated code. You don't need to rename anything.
Long namespace and type names also work with `EmitCompilerGeneratedFiles`: the generated files get short, stable
names.

Unsupported cached method shapes receive a [generator diagnostic](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md), with a code fix
to remove the cache attribute where available. Reference returns, ref struct results and pointer/function pointer
results are rejected before cached code is emitted. Those methods are forwarded when another method on the
interface is cacheable. See [keys](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/keys.md) for argument identity and
[configuration](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/configuration.md) for generated policy identifiers.

## Registration

`AddMethodCache()` wraps every registration of a cached interface in its decorator, and keeps the container's
ownership as it is: the container disposes the implementations it creates, and leaves instances you registered
yourself open. Factory registrations are wrapped the same way ([Getting started](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md#registering-with-a-factory)).

A factory registration for the README's `IUserService`, once `IUserDatabase` is registered:

```cs
builder.Services.AddScoped<IUserService>(sp =>
    new UserService(sp.GetRequiredService<IUserDatabase>()));
builder.Services.AddMethodCache();
```

`AddMethodCache` decorates the services you registered before it. A service you didn't register is registered only
with `AutoRegister(lifetime)`. The rules for keyed, generic, factory and several registrations are in
[Registration](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/reference/registration.md).

## Synchronous methods

A synchronous `[Cache]` method loads synchronously: concurrent callers with the same arguments share one call, and it
never blocks on an async load. It uses the memory cache only, also when a distributed cache is configured, so it never
waits on the network; use an async method to share results between instances. A synchronous `[CacheInvalidate]`
method clears this instance's memory before it returns, and reaches the distributed cache in the background. With
your own `ICacheManager`, which has only async operations, synchronous methods aren't cached and a warning is logged
once per method.

## Language versions

C# 12 and newer are supported with the .NET 10 SDK. With C# 13 or newer, generated decorators keep `allows ref struct`
constraints on generic methods; a type parameter that may be a ref struct, used as an argument or result, is
[MC0009](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mc0009).


---

<!-- source: docs/features/keys.md -->

# Cache keys

You never write keys for `[Cache]` methods. The generated decorator builds each key from the interface, the method
and the arguments, so two calls share an entry exactly when they call the same method with equal arguments.

Chapter 10 of the [console demo](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/samples/MethodCache.Demo) includes the tenant ID in both the key
and the invalidation tag, keeping the same product ID separate for two tenants. Derive that tenant from an
authorized identity in an application; cache-key separation does not authorize access.

```cs
public sealed record UserQuery(string Name, int Page);

public interface IUserService
{
    [Cache] Task<User> GetAsync(int id);                     // [MyApp]MyApp.IUserService.GetAsync:42
    [Cache] Task<List<User>> SearchAsync(UserQuery query);   // [MyApp]MyApp.IUserService.SearchAsync:(alice:2)
    [Cache] Task<List<User>> ByIdsAsync(int[] ids);          // [MyApp]MyApp.IUserService.ByIdsAsync:[3:1:2:3]
    [Cache] Task<int> CountAsync(Dictionary<string, int[]> filters); // [MyApp]MyApp.IUserService.CountAsync:{hash} (hashed)
}
```

Examples below assume the service assembly is named `MyApp`. Its simple name prefixes every key as `[MyApp]`;
assembly versions are excluded, so redeploying a new version preserves key identity. Closed generic argument types
also include their assembly identity. Assemblies with the same namespace/type names therefore keep separate entries.
Assembly-name characters outside letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-` are escaped as `%XXXX` UTF-16 code units.
Use `IMethodCacheKeys` to get the exact key of a call ([Building a key yourself](#building-a-key-yourself)); the admin method list shows the method ids configuration uses.

## How arguments become keys

- **Simple values** (strings, numbers, `bool`, `Guid`, dates, enums) are written as they are: `GetAsync:42`.
- **Records, classes and structs** whose public properties and fields are simple values are written field by field:
  `SearchAsync:(alice:2)`. Two records with equal values give the same key.
- **Types that implement `ICacheKeyProvider`** contribute their `CacheKeyPart`.
- **Arrays and collections** of those values are written with their count and then each element in order:
  `ByIdsAsync:[3:1:2:3]`. Records and classes inside a collection must be sealed, since an unsealed element type
  could hold a subclass with more members. A dictionary counts when its keys and values are simple values. When a
  collection's runtime type differs from its declared type (an array or a list passed as `IEnumerable<int>`), the key
  includes that type, so an array and a list with the same elements stay two entries. Unknown collection subclasses passed through a base class or interface use the key generator so their own runtime state is preserved.
- **Collection subclasses with public state**, such as a list with a tenant or scope property, use the key generator. Their keys include both that public state and the elements, including when the collection is behind a base-class property. This applies to the internal fallback generator.
- **Everything else**, such as an interface or `object` argument or a collection of collections, goes through the key
  generator. The internal default generator hashes the arguments into a key such as `CountAsync:fc08ab0d…`.
- **Framework types** are written by their value wherever they appear, not by their public properties; see
  [Framework types](#framework-types). Other framework types are a build error.
- **`nint` and `nuint`** also go through the key generator, as the 64-bit number they hold, so a value gets the same
  key in 32-bit and 64-bit processes. Their type is kept: `(nint)1`, `1` and `1L` are three keys, also inside an
  `object[]` or an `object` property.
- **Values inside hashed arguments keep their runtime type.** Where a value's type differs from the type it is declared
  as (an element of `object[]` or `List<object>`, an `object` property, a property typed as a base class or interface),
  the key records the value's version-independent assembly/type identity and all of its members: `new object[] { 1 }` and `new object[] { 1L }` get
  different keys, and so do two `Circle`s behind a `Shape` property that differ only in `Radius`.
- A `CancellationToken` parameter is never part of the key.
- Keys don't depend on the current culture: `-1`, `1.5` and dates are written the same under every culture.
- `0.0` and `-0.0` are two keys in every key form (`1 / x` tells them apart). `NaN` and the infinities work anywhere,
  also inside a hashed argument, such as `double.PositiveInfinity` as a "no limit" value in a filter record.

On .NET 10 the decorator writes simple keys into a stack buffer and looks them up without allocating.

## Types whose state is private

A type with only private state, including private fields inherited from a base class, would give every value the
same key, so the key generators refuse it with an
`InvalidOperationException` instead of returning wrong results. This holds wherever the type appears in an argument:
as the argument itself, as a property of a record, or as an element of an array, list or dictionary. Implement
`ICacheKeyProvider` on it, or give it public properties:

```cs
public sealed class TenantId(Guid value) : ICacheKeyProvider
{
    private readonly Guid _value = value;   // private state: MethodCache can't see it

    public string CacheKeyPart => _value.ToString("N");
}
```

## Framework types

Types from .NET itself often keep their value out of their public properties (`BigInteger` has `IsZero` and
`Sign`, `IPAddress.ScopeId` throws for IPv4), so writing those would give different values one key. These go through
the key generator, which writes their value, in an argument of their own or inside a record, collection or tuple:

- `Guid`, `DateTime`, `DateTimeOffset`, `TimeSpan`, `DateOnly`, `TimeOnly`
- `Half`, `Int128`, `UInt128`, `BigInteger`, `Complex`
- `Uri`, `Version`, `IPAddress` (`IPAddress.Loopback` and `IPAddress.Parse("127.0.0.1")` share a key)
- `JsonElement`, as its JSON, so `{"a":1}` and `{ "a": 1 }` share a key
- `Index`, `Range`, `Vector2`, `Vector3`, `Vector4`, `Quaternion`, `Plane`, `Matrix3x2`, `Matrix4x4`
- ASP.NET Core's `PathString`, `QueryString` and `HostString`
- arrays, collections, `Memory<T>`, `Tuple`, `ValueTuple` and `KeyValuePair` of these

Any other type from .NET itself, ASP.NET Core or Microsoft.Extensions in a key (one from an assembly named
`System.*`, `Microsoft.AspNetCore.*` or `Microsoft.Extensions.*`), such as `StringBuilder` (which can change after
the call), `CultureInfo`, `Stream`, `Type` or a delegate, is build error
[MC0019](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mc0019), also as a property of your own record. Pass a value that identifies
it, such as `culture.Name`, or wrap it in a type that implements `ICacheKeyProvider`. Other libraries' models, such
as an SDK's classes in a `Microsoft.*` namespace, are written by their public properties like your own types.

## Key construction and value serialization

Key construction belongs to the runtime. Complex arguments use the internal canonical encoder; custom key parts use
`ICacheKeyProvider`. JSON and MessagePack settings select distributed **value** serialization and do not replace the
key generator.

```cs
builder.Services.AddMethodCache(cache => cache.UseJson());
```

## Method scope

Generated keys always include the assembly simple name, interface, method, version, closed generic types, the implementation type when an interface has several registrations, and the service key of a keyed registration. An argument cannot replace that scope: `CacheKeyAttribute` and its `UseAsRawKey` flag have been removed. Use `ICacheKeyProvider` to customize one argument's part, or the manual `ICacheManager` API when supplying a complete key.

```cs
public interface IDocumentStore
{
    // The document path is an argument; the interface and method remain part of the key.
    [Cache] Task<byte[]> GetAsync(string key);
}
```

## Building a key yourself

To invalidate or inspect one entry, ask `IMethodCacheKeys` for the key of the call. Resolve it from dependency
injection; the compiler checks the call, so overloads, versions, generic methods and argument formatting can't be
gotten wrong:

```cs
var key = keys.For<IOrderService>(orders => orders.GetAsync(42));
await cache.InvalidateKeyAsync(key);   // "[MyApp]Docs.Invalidation.IOrderService.GetAsync:42"
```

```cs
// A method with a Version: "[MyApp]MyApp.IInvoiceService.GetAsync:v2:42"
var versioned = keys.For<IInvoiceService>(invoices => invoices.GetAsync(42));

// An overloaded method: "[MyApp]MyApp.IInvoiceService.FindAsync(string):INV-7"
var overload = keys.For<IInvoiceService>(invoices => invoices.FindAsync("INV-7"));
```

`For` runs the call on a stand-in that records the key the decorator would use, under the method's current policy, so
it also follows a runtime version change. The method itself never runs. The call must reach exactly one cached method;
anything else, such as a method without `[Cache]`, throws an `InvalidOperationException`. For a keyed registration,
pass its service key: `keys.For<IRates>(rates => rates.Get("EUR"), serviceKey: "ecb")`.

To work with every entry of one method, ask for its method id instead. It is the id the admin method list shows and
appsettings uses, and it covers all arguments, versions, generic arguments and keyed registrations of the method:

```cs
// "[MyApp]MyApp.IInvoiceService.FindAsync(string)": Any<T>.Value stands for any argument
var methodId = keys.MethodId<IInvoiceService>(invoices => invoices.FindAsync(Any<string>.Value));
var entries = admin.ListEntries(methodId: methodId);
```

```cs
var methodId = keys.MethodId<IInvoiceService>(invoices => invoices.FindAsync(Any<string>.Value));
var result = await admin.InvalidateMethodAsync(methodId);   // every result of the method, on every instance
```

`MethodId` reads the method from the call and never creates the service; `Any<T>.Value` stands for any argument.
`For` creates the service only to learn its type, when the interface has several registrations and the last is a
singleton factory.

`CacheEntryInfo.MethodId` tells which method an entry belongs to; it is `null` for entries stored through
`ICacheManager` directly. An application `ICacheManager` stores entries under `MethodCacheKeys.StoredKey(key, version)`;
see [Manual caching](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/manual-caching.md).

## Things to know

- **Keys contain the arguments.** Don't cache methods that take secrets such as passwords or tokens as arguments; pass
  an identifier instead. Hashed keys are not encryption. No argument, whatever characters it contains, can produce
  another call's key; see [Security](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/security.md).
- **`Version` changes every key** of a method, so values cached by an earlier version are ignored. See
  [Expiration](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/expiration.md#versions).
- **Overloaded methods** have their parameter types in their keys, so overloads never share entries. See
  [method ids](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/configuration.md#appsettingsjson).
- **A method name that another interface in the hierarchy also declares** gets the same treatment. Keys start with
  the decorated interface, so for `ICatalog : ILookup` with `ILookup.Find(int)` and `ICatalog.Find(string)` the keys
  are `[MyApp]MyApp.ICatalog.Find(int):7` and `[MyApp]MyApp.ICatalog.Find(string):7`. When two base interfaces declare the same
  signature, the declaring interface is added too: for `IC : IA, IB` that both declare `Get(int)`, the keys are
  `[MyApp]MyApp.IC.[MyApp]MyApp.IA.Get(int):1` and `[MyApp]MyApp.IC.[MyApp]MyApp.IB.Get(int):1`. Policy ids don't change; each
  method keeps the id of the interface that declares it.
- **Keyed registrations** have their service key after the method name, so `AddKeyedScoped<IRates, EcbRates>("ecb")`
  and `AddKeyedScoped<IRates, FedRates>("fed")` each cache their own results: `[MyApp]MyApp.IRates.Get@ecb:1` and
  `[MyApp]MyApp.IRates.Get@fed:1`. Other keys carry their type (`Get@[MyApp]MyApp.Region.Eu`, `Get@Int32(7)`), and a
  string with a `.`, `(` or `"` in it is written in quotes, so keys of different types never share entries. The service
  key must be a string, enum, bool, char, integer or `Guid`; `AddMethodCache()` throws for a keyed registration of a
  cached interface with any other key, and for a `KeyedService.AnyKey` registration. A constructor parameter marked
  `[ServiceKey]` receives your key, as it does without MethodCache.
- **Several registrations of one interface** under the same service key (or under none) with different
  implementation types each cache their own results. Their keys carry the implementation type before any service key:
  with `AddSingleton<IRates, EcbRates>()` and `AddSingleton<IRates, FedRates>()` the keys are
  `[MyApp]MyApp.IRates.Get#[MyApp]MyApp.EcbRates:1` and `[MyApp]MyApp.IRates.Get#[MyApp]MyApp.FedRates:1`. A single
  registration keeps the plain key. Two registrations the container builds from the same implementation type, such as
  a library and the application both calling `AddSingleton<IRates, EcbRates>()`, are interchangeable and share their
  results. An instance registration can be configured differently, so `AddMethodCache()` fails when one has the same
  type as another registration under that key; a factory that creates the same type as another registration fails
  when both have been created. Give each its own service key instead. `keys.For<IRates>(...)` returns the key of the
  last registration, the one `GetService<IRates>()` returns. When that one is a scoped or transient factory, which
  may create another type in each scope, `For` throws an `InvalidOperationException` instead of guessing: register it
  with its implementation type, give it a service key of its own, or invalidate by tag.
- **All registrations of a method share its method id and its tags.** A `[CacheInvalidate]` tag, on any registration,
  and `InvalidateMethodAsync` remove the matching entries of all of them.
- **Generic methods** carry their closed type arguments after the method name, before any implementation type or
  service key: `Get<[System.Private.CoreLib]System.Int32>:1`. Overloads that differ only in generic arity stay apart in
  ids and keys: `Get(int)`, ``Get`1(int)`` and ``Get`2(int)``. `keys.For` writes the type arguments for you, and the
  method id covers every closed type.
- To see the keys your application produces, list them with `ICacheAdministrator.ListEntries()` or the admin
  endpoints ([Monitoring](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/monitoring.md)).


---

<!-- source: docs/features/expiration.md -->

# Expiration

Each cached method decides how long its entries live. The settings below can be set on `[Cache]`, in startup code, in
`appsettings.json` or at runtime ([Configuration](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/configuration.md)).

Chapter 7 of the [console demo](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/samples/MethodCache.Demo) runs absolute expiry, sliding windows and
refresh-ahead with an explicitly advanced clock and checked source-call counts.

```cs
public interface IReportService
{
    // Gone ten minutes after it was stored
    [Cache(Duration = "00:10:00")]
    Task<Report> GetAsync(int year);

    // Kept while it is read at least every five minutes, but never longer than an hour
    [Cache(Duration = "01:00:00", SlidingExpiration = "00:05:00")]
    Task<Session> GetSessionAsync(string id);

    // Reloaded in the background when it is read in its last minute, so callers never wait
    [Cache(Duration = "00:10:00", RefreshAhead = "00:01:00")]
    Task<PriceList> GetPricesAsync(string region);

    // Changing the version changes every key, so values cached by the previous version are ignored
    [Cache(Duration = "1.00:00:00", Version = 2)]
    Task<Report> GetYearlyAsync(int year);
}
```

## Writing a duration

Attributes, `appsettings.json` and runtime configuration read durations the same way:

| Write | Means | Example |
|---|---|---|
| a number and `s` | seconds | `"30s"`, `"0.5s"` |
| a number and `m` | minutes | `"5m"`, `"1.5m"` |
| a number and `h` | hours | `"24h"`, `"1.5h"` |
| a number and `d` | days | `"1d"`, `"7d"` |
| `hh:mm:ss` or `d.hh:mm:ss` | a `TimeSpan` | `"00:05:00"`, `"1.00:00:00"` |
| `"off"` | turned off (`SlidingExpiration`, `RefreshAhead` and `FailSafe` only) | `"off"` |

- Units are case-insensitive and the number uses a `.` for decimals, whatever the culture.
- Milliseconds are written as seconds (`"0.25s"`) or as a `TimeSpan` (`"00:00:00.250"`). There is no `ms` unit.
- A bare number (`"300"`), zero, a negative value and combined units (`"1h30m"`) are errors: at build time in an
  attribute ([MC0004](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mc0004)), and at startup in `appsettings.json`.
- In code, pass a `TimeSpan`; `TimeSpan.Zero` turns `SlidingExpiration`, `RefreshAhead` or `FailSafe` off.

## Duration

`Duration` is how long an entry lives after it was stored. A method without one uses the global default:

```cs
builder.Services.AddMethodCache(config =>
    config.Defaults(o => o.WithDuration(TimeSpan.FromMinutes(15))));
```

Without any default, entries live for five minutes. No entry lives longer than
`MethodCacheMemoryOptions.MaxExpiration` (seven days), so a longer `Duration` fails where it is set instead of being
cut short: at startup, in a runtime override or in a manual call. For longer entries, raise the limit, up to 365 days,
with `mc.Memory(o => o.MaxExpiration = ...)`. With your own `ICacheManager`, its own limits apply. See
[Memory cache](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/memory-cache.md).

## Sliding expiration

`SlidingExpiration` keeps an entry while it is read: each read extends its life by the sliding window. It never lives
past its `Duration`; without a `Duration`, only `MaxExpiration` limits it.

A method that inherits a sliding window from the defaults, a group or configuration turns it off with
`SlidingExpiration = "off"` (`TimeSpan.Zero` in code). Leaving the setting out inherits it. `RefreshAhead` works the
same way.

## Refresh-ahead

`RefreshAhead` reloads an entry in the background when it is read within that window before it expires. The caller
gets the cached value at once, and the reload replaces it, so a popular entry never makes anyone wait. An entry that
isn't read in the window simply expires.

The window must be shorter than `Duration` and `SlidingExpiration`, or every read would reload the entry: on `[Cache]`
(build error [MC0023](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mc0023)), in code (`Build()` throws an `InvalidOperationException`)
and in `appsettings.json` (startup fails) a longer one is rejected.
When settings from different places combine into such a window, for example an attribute's `RefreshAhead` with a
shorter `Duration` from configuration, the reload starts halfway through the entry's life instead.

The reload outlives the request that triggered it. For a service registered as scoped or transient (a repository
with a scoped `DbContext`, say), it runs on a new instance from a new DI scope, which is disposed when the reload ends,
never on the request's instance, whose scope may already be gone. That instance has none of the request's state: no
`HttpContext`, and no values the request set on the instance or in `AsyncLocal`. Each scoped or transient cached
service the reload calls gets an instance this way, also from a manual `GetOrCreateAsync` factory, and every scope is
disposed when the reload ends; a call the factory leaves running after it returned keeps the instance it was given.
Singletons reload on their one instance. A `CancellationToken` parameter of the method still cancels the reload.

## Versions

`Version` is part of every key the method produces. Raise it when the shape of the cached result changes, for example
after adding a property, so values cached by the previous deployment are never returned. The old entries expire on
their own.

## Spreading out expiry

Entries created at the same moment, for example right after a deploy, also expire together.
`MethodCacheMemoryOptions.JitterMaxDuration` adds a random extra lifetime to each entry to spread them out
([Memory cache](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/memory-cache.md)).

## Removing entries early

> [!TIP]
> Expiration is for data that may be a little old. When you know data changed, remove it right away with
> [invalidation](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/invalidation.md).


---

<!-- source: docs/features/invalidation.md -->

# Invalidation

Expiration removes entries eventually; invalidation removes them the moment you know the data changed.

## Tags

Give cached methods tags, and list the same tags on the methods that change the data:

```cs
public interface IOrderService
{
    [Cache(Duration = "00:10:00", Tags = ["orders", "order:{orderId}"])]
    Task<Order> GetAsync(int orderId);

    [Cache(Duration = "00:05:00", Tags = ["orders", "customer:{customerId}:orders", "customer:{customerId}"])]
    Task<List<Order>> ListForCustomerAsync(int customerId);

    // Removes this order and the customer's list, nothing else
    [CacheInvalidate(Tags = ["order:{orderId}", "customer:{customerId}:orders", "customer:{customerId}"])]
    Task CancelAsync(int orderId, int customerId);

    // Removes every cached order
    [CacheInvalidate(Tags = ["orders"])]
    Task ImportAsync(Stream file);
}
```

- `[CacheInvalidate]` removes every entry with any of its tags once the method has completed successfully. If it
  throws, nothing is removed.
- A tag can be shared by many methods, so one write clears every cached view of the same data.
- `[CacheInvalidate]` without tags removes nothing and is reported as [MC0007](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mc0007).

## Tag templates

`"order:{orderId}"` is filled in from the method's arguments: `GetAsync(42)` is tagged `order:42`, and
`CancelAsync(42, 7)` removes `order:42`. The name in braces must be a parameter of the method it is on. The exact
spelling is used first; otherwise a single case-insensitive match is used. A name that matches several parameters
only by case, such as `{NAME}` for `name` and `Name`, stays literal text and is reported as
[MC0017](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mc0017). An unknown name is reported as
[MC0010](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mc0010), with a code fix that offers the closest parameter. Arguments use canonical key-part formatting: strings escape backslashes and colons, GUIDs use the 32-digit `N`
format, and null uses `\0`. Braces in an argument remain literal: an id of `"{org}"` gives
the tag `order:{org}` on both the cached call and the invalidation.

A template takes a parameter name only. `"{order.Id}"` is not a template and stays literal text, so every call would
share one tag; it is reported as [MC0016](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mc0016). Add the id as a parameter, as `UpdateAsync(int id, Product product)` does in
[Getting started](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md).

Static tags never format method arguments. A template formats only the parameters it references, in the invariant culture; an unrelated argument's `ToString()` is not invoked.

Tags set in startup code, `appsettings.json` or runtime overrides can use templates too, with any parameter of the
method. They are added to the `[Cache]` attribute's tags, so the attribute's `[CacheInvalidate]` tags keep working;
only an explicit `ClearTags()` (or `"ClearTags": true` in `appsettings.json`) replaces them
([Configuration](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/configuration.md)). An override with `o => o.AddTags("incident")` on `GetAsync` above gives its
entries the tags `orders`, `order:{orderId}` and `incident`.

`[CacheInvalidate]` also works on methods with `ref` or `ref readonly` returns, and on `Task` and `ValueTask` methods
with `ref`, `out` or `in` parameters. The tags are filled in after the call returns, and the entries are removed only
once the task has completed successfully.

## From code

`ICacheManager` invalidates by tag or by key:

```cs
await cache.InvalidateTagsAsync(["order:42", "customer:7:orders"]);
```

```cs
var key = keys.For<IOrderService>(orders => orders.GetAsync(42));
await cache.InvalidateKeyAsync(key);   // "[MyApp]Docs.Invalidation.IOrderService.GetAsync:42"
```

```cs
await cache.InvalidateTagAsync("customer:7");   // add this tag to every customer entry
```

- `IMethodCacheKeys.For` returns the key the generated decorator uses for that call, including overloads, versions,
  generic methods and keyed registrations; resolve `IMethodCacheKeys` from dependency injection. See
  [Building a key yourself](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/keys.md#building-a-key-yourself).
- Invalidation matches exact tags and keys; there are no wildcard patterns. Attach a common tag to all entries in a
  group instead.
- To remove every entry of one method, pass its id to `ICacheAdministrator.InvalidateMethodAsync`; get the id from
  `IMethodCacheKeys.MethodId` ([Cache keys](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/keys.md#building-a-key-yourself)).
- The admin endpoints and `ICacheAdministrator` also invalidate by tag and by method ([Monitoring](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/monitoring.md)).

## When the write happens somewhere else

`[CacheInvalidate]` covers writes that go through the cached interface. With Entity Framework Core,
[`MethodCache.EntityFrameworkCore`](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/entity-framework-core.md) invalidates after every commit that changes a mapped
entity, wherever the write happens. When the data changes somewhere else, such as
an endpoint or a command that writes to the database directly, or a transaction that commits after the
`[CacheInvalidate]` method has returned, invalidate after the write or the commit. Get the tag from
`IMethodCacheKeys.Tag`, so you never build it by hand:

```cs
public interface IPriceSource
{
    const string RateTag = "price:{provider}:{model}";

    [Cache(Duration = "00:05:00", Tags = [RateTag])]
    Task<decimal?> GetRateAsync(string provider, string model);
}
```

```cs
public static async Task UpdateRateAsync(string provider, string model, decimal rate,
    PriceDb db, ICacheManager cache, IMethodCacheKeys keys)
{
    await db.SaveRateAsync(provider, model, rate);   // written directly, not through IPriceSource

    // The tag GetRateAsync(provider, model) stored its result under, formatted exactly as the decorator does
    await cache.InvalidateTagAsync(
        keys.Tag<IPriceSource>(s => s.GetRateAsync(provider, model), IPriceSource.RateTag));
}
```

- `keys.Tag<T>(call, template)` fills in the template from the call's arguments exactly as the decorator does. The
  method never runs. The template must be one of the method's tags, or it throws and lists them, so a template that
  drifts away from the method fails in your tests instead of silently matching nothing. A `const` on the interface
  lets the attribute and the call share it.
- For one entry, `cache.InvalidateKeyAsync(keys.For<IPriceSource>(s => s.GetRateAsync(provider, model)))` removes
  only that call's result.
- Don't build the tag with string interpolation. Tags write arguments in one canonical way (`:` and `\` escaped in
  strings, a `Guid` without hyphens, an enum as its number), so `$"price:{provider}:{model}"` can match nothing for a
  model such as `gemma3:4b`, and the old value stays until it expires. The analyzer reports such a tag as
  [MC0024](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mc0024).
- A `[CacheInvalidate]` method with an empty body, such as `Task PriceChangedAsync(string provider, string model)`,
  works too: call it after the write.

### After a database transaction

With Entity Framework Core, [`MethodCache.EntityFrameworkCore`](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/entity-framework-core.md) does this for you. With
another way to write, such as Dapper or ADO.NET, invalidate after the transaction commits, not before and not inside it. An invalidation before the commit lets a
reader cache the old data again in between, and a rollback after it has nothing to undo. Pass
`CancellationToken.None`: once the data has changed, the invalidation must happen even if the caller has gone.

```cs
public static async Task RenameAsync(int id, string name, DbConnection connection, ICacheManager cache,
    IMethodCacheKeys keys, CancellationToken ct)
{
    await using (var transaction = await connection.BeginTransactionAsync(ct))
    {
        await using var command = connection.CreateCommand();
        command.Transaction = transaction;
        command.CommandText = "update products set name = @name where id = @id";
        AddParameter(command, "@name", name);
        AddParameter(command, "@id", id);
        await command.ExecuteNonQueryAsync(ct);
        await transaction.CommitAsync(ct);
    }

    // After the commit, and not cancelled with the request: the data has changed either way
    await cache.InvalidateTagAsync(
        keys.Tag<IProductReads>(r => r.GetNameAsync(id), IProductReads.ProductTag), CancellationToken.None);
}
```

To make a forgotten invalidation unlikely, give every write path one place to go. Put the writes behind an interface
with `[CacheInvalidate]` methods that commit their own transaction: the attribute runs after the method returns, so
after the commit, and only when it succeeded. Where writes must stay inline, wrap them in a helper that commits and
then invalidates, and test each write path with a cached read before and after it
([Testing](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/testing.md#when-a-test-writes-to-the-database-directly)).

## With several instances

With [Redis, SQL Server or PostgreSQL](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/distributed-cache.md), invalidating a tag or key removes it from the distributed
cache and sends every other instance a message to drop its in-memory copy. You don't need to do anything else, but the
other instances drop their copies when the message arrives, not when the call returns: until then they can serve the
copy they hold. How each provider catches up after a lost connection is in
[What other instances see](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/distributed-cache.md#what-other-instances-see).

The `InvalidationResult` that `InvalidateTagAsync` and `InvalidateKeyAsync` return counts how far the invalidation
got, per tag or key:

| Count | Means |
|---|---|
| `Local` | Removed from this instance's memory |
| `Distributed` | Confirmed by the distributed cache: instances without a copy in memory, and instances that start later, read the new value |
| `Queued` | Not confirmed by the distributed cache yet. It is retried every `CircuitBreakerDuration`, and until then other instances can serve the old value |
| `Published` | The message to the other instances was sent. Nothing confirms that each one received it |
| `PublicationQueued` | Confirmed by the distributed cache, but the message wasn't sent yet; it is retried |

Without a distributed cache only `Local` counts.


---

<!-- source: docs/features/entity-framework-core.md -->

# Entity Framework Core

The `MethodCache.EntityFrameworkCore` package invalidates cached results when Entity Framework Core commits a change.
Map an entity type to the tags of the methods that read it, and every save that adds, changes or deletes one of its
rows invalidates those tags, after the data is committed. Writes don't need invalidation code of their own, also when
they happen inline in an endpoint.

Install it at the same version as `MethodCache`.

## Setting it up

The cached reads are ordinary `[Cache]` methods with tags:

```cs
public interface IProductReads
{
    [Cache(Duration = "00:10:00", Tags = ["product:{id}"])]
    Task<ProductDto?> GetAsync(int id);

    [Cache(Duration = "00:10:00", Tags = ["category:{categoryId}"])]
    Task<IReadOnlyList<ProductDto>> ListAsync(int categoryId);

    [Cache(Duration = "01:00:00", Tags = ["top-sellers"])]
    Task<IReadOnlyList<ProductDto>> TopSellersAsync();
}
```

Connect the context in `AddMethodCache`, and say which tags a change to each entity type invalidates:

```cs
builder.Services.AddDbContext<ShopDb>(o => o.UseSqlite(connectionString));
builder.Services.AddScoped<IProductReads, ProductReads>();

builder.Services.AddMethodCache(mc => mc.UseEntityFrameworkCore<ShopDb>(ef => ef
    .Entity<Product>("product:{Id}", "category:{CategoryId}")
    .Entity<OrderLine>("top-sellers")));
```

`AddDbContext`, `AddDbContextPool` and `AddDbContextFactory` stay as they are, before or after `AddMethodCache`. A
save is now all a write needs:

```cs
public static async Task ChangePriceAsync(int id, decimal price, ShopDb db, CancellationToken ct)
{
    var product = await db.Products.SingleAsync(p => p.Id == id, ct);
    product.Price = price;
    // Invalidates product:{id} and category:{CategoryId} once the save succeeded
    await db.SaveChangesAsync(ct);
}
```

## Mapping entities to tags

`Entity<TEntity>(tags)` takes the tags to invalidate when a row of that type is added, changed or deleted.

- **A name in braces is a property of the entity**, also a shadow property such as a foreign key that has no property
  in the class. The exact spelling is used first; otherwise the only property that matches without regard to case.
- **Values are written as cached methods write arguments**: a `Guid` as 32 digits without hyphens, an enum as its
  number, `:` and `\` escaped in strings. So `"product:{Id}"` on the entity matches `"product:{id}"` on a method, and
  `"sku:{Sku}"` matches `"sku:{sku}"` for a SKU such as `ham:mer`.
- **A changed row invalidates the tags of its old and its new values.** Moving a product to another category
  invalidates `category:1` and `category:2`.
- **A row you change without loading it is read once before it is saved**, for its stored values. That covers
  `Update(product)` with values from a request, `Attach` with a few properties set, and `Remove(new Product { Id = id })`:
  the category it had in the database is invalidated, not the empty value of a new object. A row the context loaded
  is never read again.
- **A new row is tagged with its saved values**, so a key the database generates is the real one, not a temporary value.
  A cached "not found" for that id is invalidated too.
- **A derived type** invalidates the tags of every mapped type it derives from.
- **A type mapped with `OwnsOne` or `OwnsMany`**, such as an address stored in the customer's row, invalidates the
  tags of its owner. **A many-to-many link** added or removed invalidates the tags of both sides that are mapped.
- **A tag without braces**, such as `"top-sellers"`, is invalidated by any change to that entity type.
- **Everything the save writes counts**: rows another `SaveChanges` interceptor changes, adds or deletes, and rows EF
  Core deletes by cascade during the save.

The tags are checked against the model when the host starts. A name that is not a property, or a type the context
doesn't map, stops the host with a message that lists the entity's properties. When the context can't be created at
startup, because it needs something only a request has, the first save checks them instead.

Map each entity to the tags of every cached method whose result reads it. A method that reads several tables needs
a tag that each of their entities invalidates, such as `top-sellers` above for order lines.

Rows the database changes by itself aren't seen: rows that `ON DELETE CASCADE` removes when the context hadn't loaded
them, and rows a trigger writes. Give the cached methods that read them a tag that the parent entity invalidates too,
such as `category:{CategoryId}` on products for a method that lists a category with its products.

## When the tags are invalidated

Never before the data is committed: a reader in between would cache the old rows again.

| Situation | Invalidated |
|---|---|
| `SaveChanges` without a transaction | After it succeeds |
| Inside `BeginTransaction` | After `Commit`. `Rollback` drops them |
| Inside a `TransactionScope` | When the scope ends, also when it aborts: a connection outside the scope may have saved |
| A transaction passed in with `UseTransaction` | When a context connected to MethodCache commits it, or else once it is over: when its connection closes, or when the context is disposed after the commit |
| `SaveChanges` throws | Nothing, when nothing reached the database. When part of it may have, such as a commit that failed on the way back, its tags are invalidated |
| An execution strategy retries | A failed attempt invalidates nothing early; the retry collects its tags again |

```cs
public static async Task MoveAsync(int id, int categoryId, ShopDb db, CancellationToken ct)
{
    await using var transaction = await db.Database.BeginTransactionAsync(ct);
    var product = await db.Products.SingleAsync(p => p.Id == id, ct);
    product.CategoryId = categoryId;
    await db.SaveChangesAsync(ct);   // nothing invalidated yet: the transaction is open
    await transaction.CommitAsync(ct);   // product:{id}, the old and the new category:{CategoryId}
}
```

- Synchronous `SaveChanges()` and `Commit()` invalidate the memory cache before they return. Redis, SQL Server or
  PostgreSQL confirm in the background, so the call never waits on the network.
- An invalidation after a commit never throws: the data is saved, and an exception would make the caller think the
  save failed. If the distributed cache is down, the invalidation is retried until it is back, and logged as a warning.
- With several instances, the other instances drop their copies as with any invalidation
  ([With several instances](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/invalidation.md#with-several-instances)).
- Commit through EF Core: `Commit()` on what `BeginTransaction` returned, or `Database.CommitTransaction()`. A
  transaction that ends some other way, such as a commit on its `DbTransaction`, has its tags invalidated at the
  context's next save or when the context is disposed.
- Where the outcome is unknown, the tags are invalidated: an extra invalidation costs a cache miss, a missing one
  serves old data until it expires.

## Writes the change tracker doesn't see

`ExecuteUpdate`, `ExecuteDelete` and `Database.ExecuteSql…` change rows without loading them, so no entity tags are
known for them. Warning [MC0027](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mc0027) reports such a write when the method around it
doesn't invalidate anything, also through a call to a `[CacheInvalidate]` method.

Inside a transaction, queue the tags with `InvalidateAfterCommit`. They are invalidated with the entity tags after the
commit, and dropped on a rollback:

```cs
public static async Task RecalculateAsync(ShopDb db, IMethodCacheKeys keys, int categoryId, CancellationToken ct)
{
    await using var transaction = await db.Database.BeginTransactionAsync(ct);
    await db.Products
        .Where(p => p.CategoryId == categoryId)
        .ExecuteUpdateAsync(s => s.SetProperty(p => p.Price, p => p.Price * 1.1m), ct);
    // ExecuteUpdateAsync goes past the change tracker: name the tags it changes
    db.InvalidateAfterCommit(keys.Tag<IProductReads>(r => r.ListAsync(categoryId), "category:{categoryId}"));
    await transaction.CommitAsync(ct);
}
```

Without a transaction, the write is committed when it returns. Invalidate at once:

