```cs
var keys = provider.GetRequiredService<IMethodCacheKeys>();
await cache.InvalidateTagAsync(keys.Tag<IProductService>(p => p.GetAsync(changed.Id, default), "product:{id}"));
```

`ClearAsync` also removes the entries from a distributed cache and the other instances, so use a cache of the test's
own (a new service provider, or its own `KeyPrefix`) when tests run in parallel against a shared Redis or database.

## Turning method caching off

Register `NoOpCacheManager` after `AddMethodCache()` and every call reaches your implementation:

```cs
var services = new ServiceCollection();
services.AddSingleton<Database>();
services.AddScoped<IProductService, ProductService>();
services.AddMethodCache();
services.AddSingleton<ICacheManager, NoOpCacheManager>();   // after AddMethodCache: every call reaches ProductService
```

For code that uses [manual caching](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/manual-caching.md), pass a `NoOpCacheManager` directly, or mock the four
operations on `ICacheManager` (the short forms are extension methods that call them):

```cs
ICacheManager cache = new NoOpCacheManager();   // never caches: the factory runs on every call
var reader = new OrderReader(cache, repository);
```

`NoOpCacheManager` is in the `MethodCache` namespace. It turns off method caching only; responses of an `HttpClient`
with `AddHttpCaching` are still cached.

## Time

> [!TIP]
> The cache reads the time from the `TimeProvider` registered in the container, if there is one. Register a fake
> `TimeProvider`, for example from `Microsoft.Extensions.TimeProvider.Testing`, to test expiration without waiting.
> This includes the background cleanup of the memory cache and, with `MethodCache.HttpCaching`, response freshness,
> eviction and the background revalidation timeout.


---

<!-- source: docs/security.md -->

# Security

What each package protects against, what it leaves to you, and the tests that hold it to that.

## MethodCache (keys, tags, invalidation)

| Threat | What MethodCache does |
|---|---|
| A caller crafts an argument (`"1:orders"`, `"a)"`, a newline) so that their call gets another call's key and its cached result | Keys separate arguments unambiguously: string parts escape `\` and `:`, `null` is `\0`, records are `(a:b)` with escaped members, and hashed keys length-prefix every value and record the runtime type of values in `object`, base-class or interface slots (`1` and `1L` in an `object[]` differ). JSON and MessagePack key-provider parts and nested strings preserve exact UTF-16 code units, including lone surrogates. Building a key that itself builds keys (an `ICacheKeyProvider`, a getter) can't change another call's key. Arguments whose only state is private, including fields inherited from base classes, are rejected rather than hashed as an empty object. Framework types are written by their value (`BigInteger`, `IPAddress`, `JsonElement` and the others in [Cache keys](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/keys.md#framework-types)), not by public properties such as `BigInteger.Sign`, and any other type from .NET, ASP.NET Core or Microsoft.Extensions in a key, such as `StringBuilder`, is build error MC0019. Overloaded methods include the namespaces of their parameter types, so equally named types from different namespaces cannot share a method identity, and a method name that two interfaces of one hierarchy declare adds the parameter types (and the declaring interface for equal signatures) to the key, so `ILookup.Find(int)` and `ICatalog.Find(string)` cannot share an entry through the `ICatalog` decorator. A collection subclass's own public properties are part of the key, with its elements. No argument list produces another method's key or another argument list's key. Fluent versions have a separate namespace, with reserved user-key prefixes escaped, so a crafted raw key cannot reach a versioned entry. |
| Two service libraries declare identical namespace/type names | Generated service keys and policy ids include the assembly simple name, without its version; keyed-service enum types, closed generic arguments and fallback runtime types (including nested object values) also include assembly identity. Assembly-name delimiters are escaped. `AssemblyKeySecurityTests` and the cross-assembly SignatureCorpus regression verify separate values and overrides. Libraries with the same assembly identity are trusted as the same logical library; this is not isolation between AssemblyLoadContexts. |
| An argument that is a secret ends up readable | Keys contain argument values in plain text (hashed keys are not encryption) and appear in the admin endpoints and, if you turn them on, in traces. Don't cache methods that take passwords or tokens; pass an id. |
| A dynamic tag argument impersonates another argument | Dynamic placeholders use canonical key parts: null has its own marker, strings escape colons and backslashes, enums use invariant numbers, and dates keep their full precision. Static template text stays literal. Tags remain an application-defined shared invalidation namespace; they are not an authorization boundary. |
| A load races invalidation and a newer write | Invalidated loads cannot publish over newer entries, even when custom weight calculation stalls or re-enters the cache. Existing callers may finish with their pre-invalidation result; later loads and writes retain their own entry. |
| A tag built from user text clears the whole distributed cache | The distributed cache stores every character of a tag exactly, lone surrogates included, so a tag never turns into another one. A tag is only ever its own tag, whatever characters it holds; the internal "clear everything" marker can't be named by a tag. |
| `*` or `?` in user text widens an invalidation | `InvalidateTagsAsync`, `InvalidateKeysAsync` and admin endpoints match exact keys and tags. Group invalidation uses an explicit common tag. |
| A tenant ID is missing from the cache key or invalidation scope | The console tenant example passes an explicit `Guid` tenant ID in the method arguments and tag, and `DemoTenantSecurityTests` verifies distinct results and selective invalidation. Applications must derive and authorize that tenant from the caller's identity. |

## Distributed cache (Redis, SQL Server, PostgreSQL)

| Threat | What MethodCache does |
|---|---|
| Corrupt, truncated or crafted bytes in the distributed cache | Read as a miss and loaded again: never an exception for the caller, never a `null` that wasn't stored, and lengths in the data are checked against its size before anything is allocated. |
| Stored data names a type to create (deserialization gadgets) | `JsonCacheSerializer` reads the method's declared type and ignores `$type`. `MessagePackCacheSerializer` uses the contractless resolver with `MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData` and refuses typeless payloads. Keep it that way if you pass your own options. |
| Someone who can write to Redis, SQL Server or PostgreSQL | **Not prevented.** They can store any well-formed value, which every instance will serve. The distributed cache is trusted: protect it like your database (authentication, TLS, network rules), and give each application its own `KeyPrefix`. Different keys never share an entry: Redis escapes characters UTF-8 can't hold, and SQL Server hashes each exact key, so collation can't make two keys equal (casing, NULs, trailing spaces). SQL Server keeps each prefix's invalidations apart independently of collation too. PostgreSQL stores every key, and each prefix's backplane scope, as the SHA-256 of its exact UTF-16 code units, so NULs and lone surrogates (which PostgreSQL text can't hold) stay distinct. Its notifications carry only the sender's id; the invalidations themselves are read from the table. |
| Invalidations evicted from the store | A store that evicts a tag or removal stamp under memory pressure makes the entries it invalidated valid again (for example data cached before a permission change). Run Redis with `maxmemory-policy noeviction` or a Redis of its own; see [Keep invalidations from being evicted](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/distributed-cache.md#keep-invalidations-from-being-evicted). |
| Backplane messages | Carry keys and tags in lossless UTF-16 frames, so lone surrogates cannot change invalidation identity and newlines cannot forge another message type. Messages from another MethodCache version are rejected with one warning, without logging their contents. Anyone who can publish on the channel can invalidate entries, so the same trust applies. |

## MethodCache.AspNetCore (admin endpoints)

| Threat | What MethodCache does |
|---|---|
| An endpoint reachable without authorization | `MapMethodCacheAdmin` requires an authorization policy name, and every endpoint it maps requires that policy: anonymous callers get 401, signed-in users without it 403. A test reads the app's route table and checks every mapped endpoint, so a new endpoint without the policy fails a test. |
| The web demo is started outside Development | It requires cookie authentication and the `Admin` role, returning 401/403 for refused requests. Only Development permits anonymous admin access. `WebDemoSecurityTests` starts the actual sample and checks every admin route in both environments. The sample has no sign-in page; deployed applications must configure their own authentication. |
| Demo data can be reset outside Development | `/demo/reset` and `/demo/queries` are mapped only in Development. The sample tests verify that Production returns 404 for both. |
| A web demo price update omits a price or supplies null/negative input | The endpoint returns 400 before writing or invalidating. `WebDemoInputTests` verifies stored and cached products stay unchanged, and checks zero and the maximum decimal as valid boundaries. |
| A cross-site form or `fetch` without preflight calls `invalidate`, `invalidate-method` or `clear` with the admin's cookie | The `POST` endpoints only accept an `application/json` body, which a browser sends cross-site only after a CORS preflight; forms and `text/plain` get 415, and a request without a body 400. `DELETE entry` needs a preflight too. Don't add a CORS policy that allows these routes from other origins. |
| A filter in the wrong place empties the whole cache | Emptying everything is its own endpoint, `POST clear`, which takes only `{}`: a body with any property, such as `{ "tags": [...] }`, is 400. `invalidate` takes only `tags` and `invalidate-method` only `methodId`, and an unknown query parameter is 400 on every endpoint, so a misplaced filter is rejected instead of ignored. |
| `invalidate-method` removes another method's entries | The `methodId` must be exactly the id of a cached method, as `methods` lists it; anything else is 400 and removes nothing. Entries are matched by the method they belong to, not by a key prefix, so `GetUser` never reaches `GetUsers`. |
| Cached values leak through the admin API | Entries are listed with stored key, method id, value type, age, time to live, tags and size, never the value. Keys contain argument values (see above), so the policy should admit only operators. |
| Bad input | A missing `storedKey` or `methodId`, a `methodId` no cached method has, or an out-of-range `limit` is 400, an empty or blank tag list is 400, and keys, tags and method ids are matched literally, never as patterns. |

The health check reports counts only. If you map it with a detailed response writer, put that endpoint behind
authorization too.

## MethodCache.HttpCaching

| Threat | What MethodCache does |
|---|---|
| Two users of one `HttpClient` get each other's responses (private cache, the default) | `Authorization` and `Cookie` are part of every response's key, including values that don't parse as a credential, so each caller only gets responses fetched with their own headers. `AddHttpCaching()` disables automatic cookies on known transports after all handler configuration; `KeepCookies=true` preserves the transport and bypasses response caching, validation and stale fallback completely; explicitly supplied cookie headers isolate callers. Unknown transports, and handlers inside the primary transport, bypass caching unless explicitly verified and opted in with `AllowUnverifiedTransport`. A directly constructed cache handler also bypasses known transports with automatic cookies enabled. An empty header and no header are different callers too. Header values are individually length-framed as exact UTF-16, so a comma cannot alias multiple values and isolated surrogates cannot collapse through replacement encoding. |
| A 200 or 304 changes response privacy or variant selection | Revalidated representations are checked again: `no-store`, `Vary: *` or shared-cache `private` removes previous responses. An omitted `Vary` on a 304 keeps its previous value. A full response that can't be stored still removes the old one, and a change in which headers select a variant drops the URL's older responses without hiding a newer one. |
| A shared cache (`IsSharedCache = true`) stores a personal response | Responses marked `private`, and responses to requests with any `Authorization` header, are not stored unless they say `public`, `s-maxage` or `must-revalidate` (RFC 9111 section 3.5). |
| Stale content bypasses required validation | Response or request `no-cache` requires successful validation even with stale-while-revalidate or stale-if-error enabled; origin failures propagate. |
| A cached response hands out a session | `Set-Cookie` is never stored. The caller the origin answered gets it, including on a `304`; nobody answered from the cache does. |
| Responses that vary by a header (tenant, language) get mixed | `Vary` and `KeyHeaders` keep one response per value. `Vary: *` is never served from the cache. |
| A write leaves another caller's stale copy, or serves one caller's copy to another after it | A successful `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` or `DELETE` invalidates the URL's stored responses in the shared cache before it returns, also for clients with `KeepCookies`, and a response that was loading at the time is never stored after it. This doesn't depend on the backplane. When the invalidation can't be confirmed, the call throws `HttpCacheInvalidationException` and the cache keeps retrying; the request may have succeeded at the origin, so don't repeat it automatically. A `GET` or `HEAD` that throws it is safe to retry. |
| Two URLs share an entry | The key is the method and the full URL, with reserved characters kept escaped (`%2F`, `%3F` and `/`, `?` are different URLs). |
| A followed redirect hands one caller's response to another | The transport drops `Authorization` on a redirect and changes the URL on the same message. A response that ended at another URL or method is never stored under the URL that was requested, and entries are keyed on the request as the caller sent it, before the transport changed it. |
| A malformed `Cache-Control` hides `private` or `no-store` | A `Cache-Control` or `Vary` field the parser rejects, also next to a valid one, makes the response not storable instead of being ignored. |
| Clients that get caching from `ConfigureHttpClientDefaults` share entries | Each client's handler gets its own name, so clients (often one per tenant or API key) never read each other's entries. |
| Lost or replayed HTTP invalidation records | Invalidation records only move forward; a lost one only causes misses, and an older response never comes back. Two URLs that share a record can cause an extra miss, never a response for the wrong caller. |
| Administration becomes a body or credential leak, or a false global inventory | Administration lists only what is in this instance's memory, plus at most 1024 recently seen distributed entries without their bodies. Ids are hashes: no query string, credentials or cookies. The distributed list doesn't claim the entries still exist. An unknown id is not found. |
| An oversized response exhausts the local HTTP budget | Method and HTTP budgets evict independently. Body reads are bounded by response limits and remaining conservative HTTP cost; oversized responses remain available as streams and are not cached. |
| Crafted entries in the distributed HTTP cache | Read as a miss, with every length checked against the data. As above, whoever can write that cache can store any response. |

Not guaranteed, by design:

- In a **shared** cache, a response stored for an anonymous request is served to authorized requests for the same URL
  too, and responses that depend on cookies are shared unless the origin sends `Vary: Cookie` or `private`. That is
  what RFC 9111 specifies for a shared cache. Add `Cookie` or `Authorization` to `KeyHeaders` when your origin
  personalises without saying so.
- Anonymous callers of a private cache are one caller: they share responses.
- HTTP key hashing preserves complete UTF-16 header frames; temporary pooled buffers are cleared before reuse.
- HTTP cache diagnostics omit raw URLs, headers and exception payloads. Static configured client names remain visible.
  Application/transport instrumentation has its own logging configuration.

## MethodCache.OpenTelemetry

Core owns the `MethodCache` Meter/ActivitySource. The OpenTelemetry package only subscribes to them.

| Signal | Recorded by default | Opt-in |
|---|---|---|
| Spans | `methodcache.kind`, the static `methodcache.method` or `methodcache.http.client`, `methodcache.operation` or `methodcache.invalidation.type`, and `error.type`; no exception messages, stacks or copied HTTP/URL attributes | Core `MethodCacheTelemetryOptions.RecordCacheKeys` (SHA-256 by default, raw with `HashCacheKeys=false`); `RecordCacheTags` for application tags |
| Baggage | No library-added baggage | The app controls normal ambient .NET baggage propagation/export |
| Metrics | `methodcache.kind`, the static `methodcache.method` or `methodcache.http.client`, `methodcache.bulk`, `methodcache.result`, `methodcache.invalidation.type` and `.stage`, `methodcache.operation` and `error.type` | None: keys, tags, URLs, user ids and tenant ids never become metric dimensions |

Hashing creates stable identifiers and does not make keys anonymous. Leave identity recording disabled unless the
export destination is appropriate. Core, Redis and SQL diagnostic logs omit backend exception text because it can
contain credentials, keys or argument values. An invalid configuration reload logs the path of the setting it
rejected, never the value, and failed policy watchers log only the error type; both keep the last accepted policies. Health check failures expose exception types only. Standard
application activity parentage and baggage remain intact, including when origin code uses its ambient authorization
context; MethodCache neither adds identity baggage nor strips the application's context.

## The tests

Each row above is pinned by a test: `AdminEndpointSecurityTests` (ASP.NET Core), `HttpCacheIsolationTests`,
`HttpCacheEdgeCaseTests` and `UntrustedEntryTests` (HTTP caching), `CoreInstrumentationTests` (OpenTelemetry SDK) and `TelemetryPrivacyTests` (Core), `KeyInjectionPropertyTests` and
`DistributedCacheSecurityTests` (keys, tags and the distributed cache). The implementation-level guarantees behind these rows, and the CI and release boundaries, are in
[security internals](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/developer/security-internals.md).

<!-- source: docs/reference/registration.md -->

# Registration reference

The exact rules for how `AddMethodCache()` finds and wraps cached services, for advanced users and coding agents.
Start with [Getting started](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md#3-register-it).

## Order

- `AddMethodCache()` wraps every registration of an interface that has cached methods in its generated decorator, and
  keeps the lifetime and implementation you registered. Register cached services before it.
- A cached service registered after `AddMethodCache()` fails when the host starts, or, without a host, when its
  decorator is first created. Other services can be registered later.
- Calling `AddMethodCache()` again wraps the services added since, and leaves the existing decorators as they are.
- The container disposes the implementations it creates, and leaves instances you registered yourself open, as
  without MethodCache. A decorator is disposable only when the interface is.

## Services you didn't register

- A cached interface without a registration is registered only with `AutoRegister(lifetime)`:
  `AddMethodCache(mc => mc.AutoRegister(ServiceLifetime.Scoped))`.
- It needs exactly one accessible class that implements the interface in the generated module. None, or several, is
  an error that names the service, the module and the candidates.
- Registrations you made yourself always keep their implementation and lifetime.

## Several assemblies

- Every assembly that references `MethodCache` generates decorators for its own cached interfaces, and all of them are
  used.
- When two assemblies generate a decorator for the same interface, choose the one that wins with
  `FromAssemblyOf<SomeTypeInThatAssembly>()` (or `FromAssembly(...)`). That only settles the tie: the services the other
  assemblies generate stay cached. There is no preference by entry assembly or name, under JIT and Native AOT alike.

## Keyed registrations

- `AddKeyedScoped<IProductService, ProductService>("primary")` is cached under the same key. An interface registered
  only keyed is not also registered without one.
- The service key is part of the cache keys, so each keyed registration caches its own results. It must be a string,
  enum, `bool`, `char`, integer or `Guid` ([Keys](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/keys.md#things-to-know)).
- A catch-all registration with `KeyedService.AnyKey` is rejected, since its implementation is created for whichever key
  is requested; register concrete keys instead.
- A constructor parameter marked `[ServiceKey]` receives your key, as without MethodCache.

## Several registrations of one interface

- `AddScoped<IPriceProvider, StorePrices>()` and `AddScoped<IPriceProvider, PartnerPrices>()`, resolved as
  `IEnumerable<IPriceProvider>`, each cache their own results: the implementation type is part of their keys.
- Two registrations of the same implementation type share their results.
- `IMethodCacheKeys.For` and `Tag` use the last registration, the one `GetService` returns. When that is a scoped or
  transient factory registration among several, they throw, since the factory may create another type in each scope;
  register the implementation type, give it a service key of its own, or invalidate by tag.

## Generic interfaces

- `IRepository<User>` is cached for every closed type a class in your project implements, such as
  `UserRepository : IRepository<User>`.
- An open generic registration, `AddScoped(typeof(IRepository<>), typeof(Repository<>))`, and a closed type without a
  generated decorator give an error that names the binding, at startup or on first use without a host. Register the
  closed types instead.

## Factory registrations

A factory registration is cached like any other: register it before `AddMethodCache()`, and the decorator wraps what
your factory returns, with the lifetime you chose.

## Your own cache manager

- `services.AddSingleton<ICacheManager, MyManager>()` after `AddMethodCache()` makes the decorators use your manager.
  `NoOpCacheManager` turns caching off ([Testing](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/testing.md)).
- A keyed `ICacheManager` registration is independent of the default one, and doesn't stop `AddMethodCache()` from
  registering its own.
- Your manager stores an entry under `MethodCacheKeys.StoredKey(key, version)` of the key and version it gets, so a key
  and a version name the same entry in every operation. Keys from generated decorators already carry the method's
  version, with `version` set to `null`.
- With your own manager, which has only async operations, synchronous `[Cache]` methods aren't cached (a warning is
  logged once per method), and a synchronous `[CacheInvalidate]` method fails with `NotSupportedException`.


---

<!-- source: docs/reference/distributed.md -->

# Distributed cache reference

The exact behavior of the Redis, SQL Server and PostgreSQL providers, for advanced users and coding agents. Start with
[Distributed cache](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/distributed-cache.md) for how to use them.

## Which calls use the distributed cache

- `[Cache]` methods that return `Task<T>` or `ValueTask<T>`, and `GetOrCreateAsync`, `GetOrCreateManyAsync` and
  `TryGetAsync` on `ICacheManager`.
- **Synchronous `[Cache]` methods use the memory cache only.** None of the three providers has a synchronous API that
  can be bounded by `OperationTimeout`, so a synchronous method never blocks on the network. MethodCache logs this
  once per method. A synchronous `[CacheInvalidate]` method clears this instance's memory before it returns and stores
  the invalidation in the distributed cache and tells the other instances in the background; use an async method to
  wait for that.
- `[Cache(Distributed = false)]`, `"Distributed": false` in `appsettings.json` and `WithDistributed(false)` keep a
  method or call in memory only.

## Policies and shared entries

- Instances share a method's entries when they run it with the same settings from the attribute, startup code and
  `appsettings.json`. A runtime override that changes how a method caches (`IRuntimeCacheConfigurator`) gives that
  method entries of its own on that instance, which no other instance reads, even one with an equal override.
  Removing the override invalidates the method before the instance reads shared entries again.
- A key from `IMethodCacheKeys.For` or a manual key invalidates the entry under every policy.
- Invalidating a method (`ICacheAdministrator.InvalidateMethodAsync`) on one instance removes it on the others for
  every keyed registration and every closed generic type, without changing their settings.
- A value loaded before an invalidation is never stored after it, also when the write lands after a timeout and retry.
- Each entry remembers when its load started and when it expires. Reading it applies the reading instance's
  `CacheNullValues` and `CacheWhen`, and never keeps it longer than its own `Duration` from when it was first stored, or
  `MaxExpiration`. A slow method doesn't use up the entry's duration.

## Backplanes

- **Redis** sends each invalidation with pub/sub, which reaches the instances connected at that moment. After a lost
  connection, an instance clears its memory cache once it is subscribed again. Reconnecting retries with a delay that
  doubles from one second to 30 seconds; the health check reports connected only once the subscription is confirmed.
  Shutdown stops pending retries, and a cancelled send or unsubscribe never fails shutdown.
- **SQL Server** stores invalidations in a table that each instance polls (`BackplanePollingInterval`, one second).
  Identity values are handed out before a transaction commits, so a row can appear after later ones were read; an
  instance checks the ids it skipped again, without waiting on locks, so a long transaction never holds back newer
  invalidations. The table needs a `binary(32) NOT NULL` `Scope` column
  ([SQL Server guide](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/src/MethodCache.SqlServer/README.md#required-backplane-schema)).
- **PostgreSQL** stores invalidations in a table as SQL Server does, and announces each one with `NOTIFY`, so the
  others read it at once. Ids are handed out in commit order, so there are no gaps to check. The listening connection
  reconnects with the same doubling delay and reads what it missed; until then polling delivers every invalidation.
- With `EnableBackplane = false`, another instance keeps an invalidated value in memory until it expires.
- Disposing the service provider unsubscribes. A backplane that doesn't answer delays shutdown by at most twice
  `OperationTimeout`.
- A message from another MethodCache version is ignored, with one warning. A damaged message makes the instance clear
  its memory cache, with one warning that leaves out the message's contents.

## Invalidation results

`InvalidateKeysAsync` and `InvalidateTagsAsync` check the whole batch first, and count each distinct key or tag once:

- `Requested` and `Local` count every target, also ones that weren't cached.
- With a distributed cache, `Distributed` (stored) plus `Queued` (to be retried) equals `Requested`.
- With a backplane, `Published` counts sent messages and `PublicationQueued` the stored targets whose message will be
  sent again. A sent message doesn't confirm that every instance received it.

## Cancellation

- Cancelling a call stops its wait while it reads the distributed cache, runs a slow method or waits for a fail-safe
  value, also in bulk reads. Work other callers share may finish for them. A cancelled call is not counted as a
  failure of the distributed cache.
- Cancelling an invalidation before it starts changes nothing. Once it has started, cancelling stops the caller's wait;
  the cache finishes the invalidation and retries what it couldn't store. Storage and message retries have separate,
  bounded queues, which `ICacheAdministrator.GetInvalidationQueues()` and the health check report.

## Serialization

- Every value an instance writes is first read back and written again. When that doesn't give the same bytes and type,
  that value and every later value of that method and type stay in memory only, and one warning names them. Each
  value is checked, since one with default data (an `Id` of 0 behind a private setter) can come back unchanged where
  the next one doesn't.
- That happens with properties that have a private or protected setter, public readonly fields of a type that also
  has a parameterless constructor, a derived type returned as its declared base type (an `Animal` method returning a
  `Dog`), `object`, and values the serializer throws on (a cycle, a delegate), with JSON and MessagePack alike.
- State the serializer never writes (data only in private fields, which JSON writes as `{}`) reads back as the same
  bytes, so the check can't see that it is lost. The check also looks only at the value's own type: a `Dog` inside a
  `List<Animal>` is shared without its `Dog` data. Make such state serializable, or register a serializer that writes
  it, with `UseJson(options)` or `UseJson(context)` (`[JsonInclude]`, `[JsonDerivedType]`).
- A collection declared as an interface (`IReadOnlyList<int>`) may come back as another implementation, such as a
  `List<int>` for an array, and is still shared.
- A serializer that never writes the same bytes twice (encryption with a fresh nonce) can't be compared, so only the
  type is checked. `VerifyRoundTrip = false` turns the check off.
- The options you pass to `UseJson` are copied, so changing them later has no effect.

## Storage, schemas and compatibility

- `KeyPrefix` and the connection settings are fixed when the container is built; use a new container to change them.
- The first instance that uses a prefix fixes its minimum `TagRetention`. A later instance may ask for longer, not
  shorter; a shorter setting fails at startup. Use a new prefix to lower it.
- Entries are stored per value format and `SerializerVersion`, so switching between JSON and MessagePack, or raising
  `SerializerVersion`, makes old entries misses. Invalidations apply to every format.
- An entry's expiry is fixed from when its load started, so a slow write can't extend it.
- SQL Server and PostgreSQL create their tables on first use (`CreateTablesIfMissing`), and refuse a schema they don't
  know instead of changing it. SQL Server ships `migrations/0001-version-existing-schema.sql` for an invalidations
  table from before 1.0: stop the old instances, back up the database and run it before starting the new version.
  PostgreSQL ships `migrations/0001-create-schema.sql` for logins that may not create tables.
- `ConnectionStringFactory` is resolved once from dependency injection. PostgreSQL's `ConfigureDataSource` logs in
  with a token from Microsoft Entra ID or AWS IAM
  ([Passwordless login](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/src/MethodCache.PostgreSql/README.md#passwordless-login)).
- How each provider stores its data and messages is described for contributors in
  [the storage format](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/developer/distributed-wire-v1.md).


---

<!-- source: docs/reference/http-caching.md -->

# HTTP caching reference

The exact behavior of `MethodCache.HttpCaching`, for advanced users and coding agents. Start with
[HTTP response caching](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/http-caching.md).

## Variants

- Responses are selected by the `Vary` header fields and the configured `KeyHeaders`, compared case-insensitively.
  A private cache always keeps `Authorization` and `Cookie` apart.
- Every variant of a URL is kept for at most 365 days; each expires at its own lifetime.
- When a response changes which headers select its variants, the URL's earlier variants are no longer used, once. The
  current response still reaches its caller, and the next request stores the new variant. If removing the old entry
  fails, a foreground request reports the error, and background revalidation logs it.

## Replacing a stored response

- A full response replaces the stored one. When it can't be stored (`no-store`, `private` in a shared cache, a body
  over the size limit, or a failed write), the old one is removed, so the next caller never falls back to an older
  body.
- Stale-while-revalidate respects the request's `max-age`, `min-fresh` and `max-stale`.
- The `Age` header is corrected by the request and response delay, for first responses and for 304s, and very large
  values can't overflow.
- Background revalidation sends the request with its HTTP version, version policy and a shallow copy of its request
  options. Use option values that stay valid after the original request has finished.

## Invalidation details

- Invalidating a URL starts a new generation for it; responses stored under an older generation are no longer read.
  With Redis, SQL Server or PostgreSQL the generations are stored there, so they don't depend on the backplane.
- URLs share 4096 generation slots per `KeyPrefix`, so the stored data stays bounded. Two URLs in one slot can cause an
  extra miss when either is invalidated. A lost generation record only causes misses, never an older response.
- If reading the generation fails, the request goes to the origin.
- Cancelling the caller stops its wait; the cache finishes the invalidation. Disposing the service provider
  asynchronously waits for pending invalidations and retries queued ones once. Any it can't confirm are logged as a
  count; other instances may then serve old responses until they expire.
- Invalidating the client's own tag scans the responses in memory, so its cost grows with their number. URL and
  configured tags use indexes.

## Administration

- `ICacheAdministrator` lists the responses in memory, or with a distributed cache up to 1024 responses this instance
  has seen there (`Storage = ObservedDistributed`): not proof that they are still stored, nor a list of everything
  stored. Ids are hashes; an unknown id returns NotFound.
- Removing an id removes every variant of its URL. `ClearAsync` removes every response.
- HTTP administration and byte statistics also work with `NoOpCacheManager` for methods.
- A client's tag is `http:` followed by `MethodCacheKeys.Part(clientName)` for names up to 128 UTF-16 code units;
  longer names use `http:#:` followed by the SHA-256 of the name, and administration shows the start of the name and
  its hash. `HttpCacheOptions.Tags` takes at most 125 non-blank tags of at most 1024 code units; other values fail at
  startup.
- HTTP entries have their own format: method serializers, durations, jitter and fail-safe settings don't apply to them.


---

<!-- source: docs/troubleshooting.md -->

# Troubleshooting

> [!TIP]
> To see what is actually cached, list the entries with `ICacheAdministrator.ListEntries()` or `GET /methodcache/entries`,
> and the effective policy of every method with `GetMethods()` or `GET /methodcache/methods` ([Monitoring](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/monitoring.md)).

## The method runs on every call

- **The attribute is on the class.** `[Cache]` is read from the interface only. The analyzer reports
  [MC0001](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mc0001) and its code fix moves the attribute.
- **A late or unsupported registration raises a named binding error.** Register cacheable services before
  `AddMethodCache()`. Open generic registrations such as `AddScoped(typeof(IRepository<>), ...)` are rejected;
  register generated closed types ([Getting started](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md#3-register-it)).
- **The caller doesn't use the interface.** The cache is a decorator around the interface. Resolving or injecting the
  class itself, or calling the method from inside the class (`this.GetAsync(...)`), skips it.
- **The arguments differ between calls.** A `DateTime.Now`, a new `Guid` or a request object with a unique id in it
  makes every key different. List the keys to check ([Cache keys](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/keys.md)).
- **`StringBuilder`, `CultureInfo` or another framework type in an argument** is build error
  [MC0019](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mc0019): its key would not follow its value. Pass a string or an id instead
  ([Cache keys](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/keys.md#framework-types)).
- **The result is not stored on purpose:** a `CacheWhen` predicate rejected it, the result is `null` with
  `CacheNullValues = false`, or the call threw. Exceptions are never cached.
- **A test registered `NoOpCacheManager`**, which never caches ([Testing](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/testing.md)).

## Old data after an update

- **The tags don't match.** `[CacheInvalidate]` removes only the tags it lists. Compare them with the cached methods'
  tags.
- **A tag template isn't filled in.** The name in braces must be a parameter of that method:
  [MC0010](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mc0010) warns about unknown names. A property path such as `"{product.Id}"` is
  not a template and stays literal ([MC0016](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mc0016)); pass the id as a parameter.
- **The update method threw.** Invalidation runs only after the method completes successfully.
- **The data changed outside the interface**, for example in another service or a database job. Invalidate from that
  code with `ICacheManager.InvalidateTagsAsync` ([Invalidation](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/invalidation.md#from-code)).
- **You run several instances** with only the in-memory cache. Each instance has its own cache; add
  [Redis, SQL Server or PostgreSQL](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/distributed-cache.md) with its backplane, so invalidations reach all of them.
  The application's `IDistributedCache` is not a MethodCache provider.
- **Fail-safe returned an expired value** because the method failed ([Fail-safe](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/fail-safe.md)).

## Results stay out of the distributed cache

A method whose result type is `object`, an interface or an abstract class (`Task<IShape>`, `Task<List<object>>`) has
warning [MC0020](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mc0020). The serializer can't tell which class to create when it reads
such a result back, so when a distributed cache is used the default round-trip check keeps these results in memory
only, and each instance loads its own. Return a concrete type, such as `Task<Circle>` or `Task<List<Product>>`.

## Keys look different than expected

List the keys with `ICacheAdministrator.ListEntries()` or `GET /methodcache/entries`, and get the key you expect from
`IMethodCacheKeys.For<IUserService>(users => users.GetUserAsync(42))` to compare them. `ListEntries(methodId: ...)`
lists the entries of one method only. [Cache keys](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/keys.md) explains how each argument becomes part of a
key.

## A change in appsettings.json has no effect

- `AddMethodCache(mc => mc.FromConfiguration(builder.Configuration))` must be called.
- The key under `Methods` must be the method id: the assembly name in brackets, the interface's full name, a dot and
  the method name, such as `[MyApp]MyApp.IUserService.GetUserAsync`. An unknown id fails at startup and suggests the
  closest one. `GET /methodcache/methods` lists the ids.
- A group's settings go under `Groups`, by the exact (case-sensitive) group name.
- A runtime override for the method wins over the file ([Configuration](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/configuration.md)).
- An invalid value in a reloaded file is logged as an error naming the setting, and the previous policies stay.

## Exceptions

| Exception | Cause |
|-----------|-------|
| `InvalidOperationException` when building a key | An argument type has only private state, so every value would get the same key. Implement `ICacheKeyProvider` ([Cache keys](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/keys.md#types-whose-state-is-private)) |
| `InvalidOperationException` from `AddMethodCache` naming two assemblies | Multiple generated modules contain the same interface; choose the one that wins with `FromAssemblyOf<T>()` ([Caching third-party code](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/third-party.md)) |
| `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` from `WithDuration` | Durations must be positive. Use `WithEnabled(false)` to disable caching, including in runtime overrides |
| `InvalidOperationException` at startup naming a `MethodCache:` path | An invalid value, an unknown setting name (such as a `Services` section from 1.0.0-rc.1: it is now `Methods`), a single value for `Tags`, `Metadata` or a section that holds settings, nested settings under a single setting, an invalid duration, an unknown method id, the same method listed twice, `Group`, `Metadata` or `Notes` in `Defaults` or a group, or a tag template that names no parameter of a method it reaches; positive invariant unit durations such as `30s` are supported |
| `InvalidOperationException` at startup about `CacheWhen` | `CacheWhen` was set in `Defaults` or a group; set it for one method with `mc.Method(...).CacheWhen(...)`. Or a `CacheWhen<T>` is for a type the method can't return; a runtime override with one throws an `ArgumentException` ([Conditional caching](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/conditional-caching.md)) |
| `InvalidOperationException` at startup: the `Duration` is longer than `MethodCacheMemoryOptions.MaxExpiration` | A `Duration` in `[Cache]`, code or `appsettings.json` is longer than the memory cache keeps an entry (7 days by default). Shorten it, or raise the limit with `mc.Memory(o => o.MaxExpiration = ...)`. A runtime override throws an `ArgumentException`, and a manual call an `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` before its factory runs ([Expiration](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/expiration.md)) |
| `InvalidOperationException` from `IMethodCacheKeys.For` saying it can't tell which key to return | The interface has several registrations and the last is a scoped or transient factory, which may create another type in each scope. Register it with its implementation type, give it a service key of its own, or invalidate by tag ([Cache keys](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/keys.md#building-a-key-yourself)) |
| `InvalidOperationException` from `GetOrCreateManyAsync`: the bulk factory did not return a value for a key | The factory must return a value for each key it is asked for. Nothing it returned is cached; keys with a fail-safe value get it ([Manual caching](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/manual-caching.md)) |
| `InvalidOperationException` from `AddMethodCache` naming an implementation type | An instance registration of a cached interface has the same type as another registration under the same service key. Give each its own service key ([Cache keys](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/keys.md#things-to-know)) |
| `InvalidOperationException` from `AddMethodCache` naming two distributed caches | More than one of `UseRedis`, `UseSqlServer` and `UsePostgreSql` was called; use one |

## A caller changed a cached object, and others see the change

> [!WARNING]
> The cache hands the same instance to every caller. Return immutable types such as records, or copies
> ([Memory cache](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/memory-cache.md#cached-objects-are-shared)).

## Build errors and warnings

Every `MC` diagnostic, with what to do about it, is in [Build diagnostics](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md).


---

<!-- source: docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md -->

# Build diagnostics

MethodCache checks your attributes when you build. An error stops the build: the attribute asks for something
MethodCache can't do, such as caching a `void` method, or a setting is invalid. A warning lets the build go on: the
attribute is ignored, such as `[Cache]` on a class member or on a `static` interface member, or it probably doesn't do
what you meant, such as a tag placeholder that matches no parameter. Every diagnostic links to its section below, and
the ones marked **Code fix** can be fixed from the light bulb in Visual Studio, Rider or VS Code. When both the
generator and the analyzer run, each problem is reported once.

| Id | Severity | Summary | Code fix |
|----|----------|---------|----------|
| [MC0001](#mc0001) | Warning | `[Cache]` or `[CacheInvalidate]` on a class member | Move to the interface |
| [MC0004](#mc0004) | Error | A time span that is not a positive `TimeSpan` | |
| [MC0003](#mc0003) | Error | `[Cache]` on a `void` method | Remove `[Cache]` |
| [MC0022](#mc0022) | Error | `[Cache]` on `Task`/`ValueTask` without a result | Remove `[Cache]` |
| [MC0005](#mc0005) | Error | `[Cache]` with reference parameters or returns | Remove `[Cache]` |
| [MC0006](#mc0006) | Error | `[Cache]` and `[CacheInvalidate]` on the same method | |
| [MC0007](#mc0007) | Warning | `[CacheInvalidate]` without tags | |
| [MC0008](#mc0008) | Error | `[Cache]` with pointer or function pointer parameters or returns, including arrays of them | Remove `[Cache]` |
| [MC0009](#mc0009) | Error | `[Cache]` with ref struct or potentially ref-like parameters or returns | Remove `[Cache]` |
| [MC0010](#mc0010) | Warning | A tag names a parameter the method does not have | Use the closest parameter |
| [MC0011](#mc0011) | Error | `[assembly: CacheInterface]` names a type it can't decorate | |
| [MC0012](#mc0012) | Error | `[assembly: CacheInterface]` lists a method it can't cache | |
| [MC0013](#mc0013) | Error | The same interface in more than one `[assembly: CacheInterface]` | |
| [MC0014](#mc0014) | Error | An interface with static or non-public abstract members | |
| [MC0015](#mc0015) | Error | `[Cache]` on a lazy sequence | Remove `[Cache]` |
| [MC0016](#mc0016) | Warning | A tag placeholder that is not a parameter name, such as `{product.Id}` | |
| [MC0017](#mc0017) | Warning | A tag placeholder matches several parameter names without an exact spelling match | |
| [MC0018](#mc0018) | Warning | `[Cache]` or `[CacheInvalidate]` on a `static`, non-public or `sealed` interface member | |
| [MC0019](#mc0019) | Error | A key argument, element or member has a framework type without a key form, such as `StringBuilder` | |
| [MC0020](#mc0020) | Warning | A cached result type of `object`, an interface or an abstract class, which a distributed cache can't restore | |
| [MC0021](#mc0021) | Error | An explicitly negative cache version | |
| [MC0023](#mc0023) | Error | `RefreshAhead` not shorter than `Duration` or `SlidingExpiration` on the same attribute | |
| [MC0024](#mc0024) | Warning | A value in a hand-built tag is written differently from MethodCache's tags | Format with `MethodCacheKeys.Part` |
| [MC0025](#mc0025) | Warning | A cached result type that isn't safe to share between callers, such as `JsonObject`, `DataTable` or `Stream` | |
| [MC0026](#mc0026) | Warning | The implementation of a cached interface takes per-request state, such as `IHttpContextAccessor` or `ClaimsPrincipal` | |
| [MC0027](#mc0027) | Warning | `ExecuteUpdate`, `ExecuteDelete` or raw SQL writes past EF Core's change tracker without an invalidation | |

## MC0001

`[Cache]` or `[CacheInvalidate]` is on a class, struct or record member. MethodCache generates a decorator for the
interface, so it only reads attributes on interface methods, and this one is ignored.

```csharp
public interface IUserService
{
    [Cache(Duration = "00:05:00")]      // here
    Task<User> GetAsync(int id);
}

public class UserService : IUserService
{
    public Task<User> GetAsync(int id) => ...;   // not here
}
```

**Code fix:** moves the attribute to the interface method the member implements (adding the `using` if needed), or
removes it when the member implements no interface. To cache an interface you don't own, see the
[third-party caching page](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/third-party.md).

## MC0004

`Duration`, `SlidingExpiration`, `RefreshAhead`, `FailSafe`, `FailSafeTimeout` or `FailSafeRetryAfter` on `[Cache]` or
`[assembly: CacheInterface]` is not a positive time span. Use the `TimeSpan` format: `"00:05:00"` (five minutes),
`"01:00:00"` (an hour) or `"1.00:00:00"` (a day). `SlidingExpiration`, `RefreshAhead` and `FailSafe` also accept `"off"`.

## MC0003

`[Cache]` on a `void` method: there is no result to cache. Return the value, or remove `[Cache]`. If the method
changes data, you probably want `[CacheInvalidate(Tags = ...)]` instead.

## MC0022

`[Cache]` on a method returning `Task` or `ValueTask` without a result. Return `Task<T>` or `ValueTask<T>`, or remove
`[Cache]`. A write method usually wants `[CacheInvalidate(Tags = ...)]` instead.

## MC0005

`[Cache]` on a method with `ref`, `out` or `in` parameters, or a `ref` / `ref readonly` return.
A cached value cannot preserve references or set an `out` value. Pass and return values by value, for example as a record.

## MC0006

`[Cache]` and `[CacheInvalidate]` on the same method. A method either reads (cached) or writes (invalidates); keep
the one that matches what it does.

## MC0007

`[CacheInvalidate]` without tags removes nothing. List the tags of the cached methods it should clear:

```csharp
[Cache(Tags = new[] { "users", "user:{id}" })]
Task<User> GetAsync(int id);

[CacheInvalidate(Tags = new[] { "users", "user:{id}" })]
Task UpdateAsync(int id, User user);
```

## MC0008

`[Cache]` on a method with pointer or function pointer parameters or returns, including arrays of them such as
`int*[]`. These cannot be stored as cached values or keys; use a value or an array of values. Unsupported methods, and
any other member of the interface that uses a pointer, are still forwarded through an unsafe implementation.

## MC0009

`[Cache]` on a method with `Span<T>`, `ReadOnlySpan<T>` or other ref struct parameters or returns. These cannot be
stored in a cache; use an array, `Memory<T>` or a string. This also applies to a type parameter with `allows ref struct` when that parameter is used as an argument or return value.

## MC0010

A tag such as `"user:{userId}"` names a parameter the method does not have, so the braces stay literal text and every
call shares that tag. The name between the braces must match a parameter name: the exact spelling first, otherwise a
single case-insensitive match. A name that matches several parameters only by case is [MC0017](#mc0017).

A template takes a parameter name only; a property path such as `"{product.Id}"` is reported as [MC0016](#mc0016).

**Code fix:** offers the closest parameter names, so `"user:{usrId}"` becomes `"user:{userId}"`.

## MC0011

`[assembly: CacheInterface]` names a type MethodCache can't decorate: a class, a generic interface, an interface that
is not accessible, one with static abstract or non-public abstract members, or one declared in your own project (put `[Cache]` on its methods
instead). It is also reported when the attribute lists no methods. See the [third-party caching page](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/third-party.md).

## MC0012

`[assembly: CacheInterface]` lists a method that is missing, overloaded or static, or one that `[Cache]` would reject:
it returns nothing to cache, has `ref`, `out`, `in`, pointer or ref struct parameters, a framework type without a key
form ([MC0019](#mc0019)), or returns a lazy sequence. Use
`nameof(IClient.Method)` so a rename is caught by the compiler. See the
[third-party caching page](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/third-party.md).

## MC0013

The same interface is listed in more than one `[assembly: CacheInterface]`. List each interface once, with all its
methods in the same attribute.

## MC0014

The interface has static abstract members, or non-public abstract members that cannot be forwarded to the decorated
instance. Move the cached methods to an interface without them. Non-public default methods are supported because they
remain on the interface, and so are nested helper types declared inside the interface.

## MC0015

`[Cache]` on a method returning `IEnumerable<T>`, `IAsyncEnumerable<T>` or `IQueryable<T>`. The cached value would be
the lazy sequence itself, which runs the query again on every enumeration. Return a materialized collection, such as
`Task<List<T>>`, `Task<IReadOnlyList<T>>` or `T[]`, and call `ToListAsync()` (or similar) in the implementation.

## MC0016

A tag has braces that look like a template but don't hold a plain parameter name: a property path such as
`"product:{product.Id}"`, spaces such as `"{ id }"`, or a format such as `"{day:yyyy-MM-dd}"`. Templates take a
parameter name only, so the braces stay literal text and every call shares the same tag. Write `"product:{id}"` and
add the value as its own parameter, as `UpdateAsync(int id, Product product)` does in
[Getting started](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md). For `[assembly: CacheInterface]` both MC0010 and MC0016 are reported on the
attribute.

## MC0017

The placeholder has no exact parameter match and more than one case-insensitive match, such as `{NAME}` for
parameters `name` and `Name`. Use the intended parameter's exact spelling. Until corrected, the placeholder remains
literal in both cached tags and invalidation.

## MC0018

`[Cache]` or `[CacheInvalidate]` is on an interface member the decorator can't intercept: a `static` member, a
`private` or other non-public member with a body, or a `sealed` one. The decorator implements the interface for a
class, and a class can't implement those members, so calls to them never reach the cache and the attribute does
nothing. Put the attribute on a public interface method without `static`, `private` or `sealed` (one without a body,
or a public default method), or remove it.

## MC0019

A key argument has a type from .NET itself, ASP.NET Core or Microsoft.Extensions (an assembly named `System.*`,
`Microsoft.AspNetCore.*` or `Microsoft.Extensions.*`) that the cache key can't be written from: the
argument itself, an element of a collection or tuple, or a public property or field of your own type, such as
`StringBuilder`, `CultureInfo`, `Stream`, `Type` or a `Func<T>`. Their public properties don't hold their value, or the
value can change after the call (a `StringBuilder`), so two different arguments could share a key and one caller
would get another's result. The message names the value, such as `'note.Text' is a 'StringBuilder'`.

Pass a value that identifies it instead, such as a string, an id or a culture name, or wrap it in a type that
implements `ICacheKeyProvider` (see [Cache keys](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/keys.md#framework-types)). Every argument must have a supported key form.

Framework types with a key form are written by their value: `Guid`, `DateTime`, `DateTimeOffset`, `TimeSpan`,
`DateOnly`, `TimeOnly`, `Half`, `Int128`, `UInt128`, `BigInteger`, `Complex`, `Uri`, `Version`, `IPAddress` and
`JsonElement` (as its JSON, so whitespace doesn't count), `Index`, `Range`, `Vector2`, `Vector3`, `Vector4`,
`Quaternion`, `Plane`, `Matrix3x2`, `Matrix4x4`, and ASP.NET Core's `PathString`, `QueryString` and `HostString`, as
well as arrays, collections, `Memory<T>`, tuples and `KeyValuePair` of those. Models from other libraries, such as
an SDK's classes in a `Microsoft.*` namespace, are not framework types: they are written by their public properties
like your own.

## MC0020

The cached method's result type, after `Task<T>` or `ValueTask<T>`, is `object`, an interface such as `IComparable` or
`IShape`, or an abstract class, or has one as an element (`List<object>`). A distributed cache stores results as
JSON or MessagePack of the declared type, which can't say which class to create when it reads them back. When a
distributed cache is used, the default round-trip check finds that such a result doesn't read back, and keeps it in the
in-memory cache only. Collection interfaces such as
`IReadOnlyList<Product>` are fine; they are read back as a list.

Return a concrete type, such as `Task<Product>` or `Task<List<Product>>`, to share the results through the distributed
cache. When only the in-memory cache is used, or memory-only is what you want, suppress the warning with
`#pragma warning disable MC0020` or `<NoWarn>` in the project.

## MC0021

An explicitly supplied `Version` is negative. Omit it to inherit the configured version or use a non-negative integer.

## MC0023

`RefreshAhead` on `[Cache]` or `[assembly: CacheInterface]` is as long as the `Duration` or `SlidingExpiration` next to
it, or longer. The refresh window starts that long before an entry expires, so every hit would reload the value. Use a
window shorter than both, such as `Duration = "00:10:00", RefreshAhead = "00:01:00"`, or `"off"` to turn refresh-ahead
off.

## MC0024

A tag built with string interpolation for `InvalidateTagAsync`, `InvalidateTagsAsync` or `InvalidateAfterCommit` contains a value that
interpolation writes differently from the tags MethodCache stores, so the invalidation can match nothing and the old
value stays cached, without an error:

```cs
// The cached entry is tagged price:ollama:gemma3\:4b, so this removes nothing
await cache.InvalidateTagAsync($"price:{provider}:{model}");
```

Tag templates write values in one canonical way: `:` and `\` escaped in strings, a `Guid` as 32 digits without
hyphens, an enum as its number, `true` and `false` in lower case, and numbers and dates in the invariant culture
(dates in ISO 8601). Whole numbers come out the same, so `$"user:{id}"` with an `int` is not reported.

Build the tag from a call to the cached method instead, so the template and the formatting come from the method:

```cs
await cache.InvalidateTagAsync(keys.Tag<IPrices>(s => s.GetRateAsync(provider, model), "price:{provider}:{model}"));
```

Or format each value with `MethodCacheKeys.Part`, which the code fix does:
`$"price:{MethodCacheKeys.Part(provider)}:{MethodCacheKeys.Part(model)}"`.
A value with a format such as `{price:F2}` has no fix, since the tag MethodCache stores has no format.

## MC0025

The cached method returns a type whose instances change while they are read or used, or has one as an element:
`JsonNode` and its subclasses (`JsonObject`, `JsonArray`), `DataTable`, `DataSet`, `DataRow`, `DataView`, a `Stream`
or a `StringBuilder`. The cache hands the same instance to every caller, at the same time. A `JsonNode` parses its
content lazily the first time it is read, and isn't thread-safe while it does, so two requests reading one cached
`JsonObject` at once can get an empty or broken result. A stream's position moves as one caller reads it.

```cs
[Cache(Duration = "00:05:00")]
Task<JsonObject> GetLayoutAsync(string locale);   // MC0025: every caller shares one JsonObject
```

Return an immutable type instead: a record, a string (`node.ToJsonString()`), a `byte[]` you never change, or a
`JsonElement` (`JsonDocument.Parse(json).RootElement.Clone()`), which is read-only and safe to share.
Collections such as `List<T>` and arrays are not reported: they are safe to read from several threads, but don't change
a cached one ([cached objects are shared](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/memory-cache.md#cached-objects-are-shared)).

## MC0026

A class implements an interface with `[Cache]` methods and takes per-request state in its constructor:
`IHttpContextAccessor`, `HttpContext`, `HttpRequest`, `ClaimsPrincipal` or another `IPrincipal`.

The cache key is built from the method's arguments only. A result that depends on the current request or user, such
as a query filtered by row-level security on a connection set up for that user, is stored under a key that doesn't
name the user, and the next caller gets it, whoever they are. Refresh-ahead and fail-safe also load values outside
the request, in a new scope with no `HttpContext`.

```cs
public sealed class Orders(IHttpContextAccessor http, AppDb db) : IOrders   // MC0026
{
    public Task<List<Order>> MineAsync() => db.Orders.Where(o => o.UserId == http.HttpContext!.User.Id()).ToListAsync();
}
```

Make what the result depends on a parameter of the cached method, so it becomes part of the key:
`Task<List<Order>> ForUserAsync(int userId)`, called with the current user's id. Or don't cache the method.
See [Getting started](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md#per-user-data).

## MC0027

Reported in a project that uses `MethodCache.EntityFrameworkCore`, on `ExecuteUpdate`, `ExecuteDelete`,
`ExecuteSql`, `ExecuteSqlRaw` or `ExecuteSqlInterpolated` (and their `Async` versions). They change rows without
loading them, so EF Core's change tracker never sees the rows, and no entity tags are invalidated for them. Cached
results that read those rows stay until they expire.

```cs
await db.Products.Where(p => p.CategoryId == id).ExecuteUpdateAsync(s => s.SetProperty(p => p.Price, 0m));   // MC0027
```

Invalidate the tags of the rows it changes, in the same method or in a method around it, such as the one that runs an
execution strategy: inside a transaction with `db.InvalidateAfterCommit(...)`, or after a write that is already
committed with `ICacheManager.InvalidateTagsAsync(...)`
([Writes the change tracker doesn't see](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/entity-framework-core.md#writes-the-change-tracker-doesnt-see)).
A call to a `[CacheInvalidate]` method of a cached interface counts as an invalidation. The warning is not reported
in the implementation of a `[CacheInvalidate]` method either, which invalidates its own tags.
When nothing cached reads the rows, turn it off for that line with `#pragma warning disable MC0027`.


---

<!-- source: docs/migration-from-imemorycache.md -->

# Migrating from IMemoryCache

With `IMemoryCache`, every cached method holds the same pattern: build a key, try the cache, load, store, and remember
every key to remove when data changes. MethodCache moves that into an attribute on the interface.

<table>
<tr><th>Before: IMemoryCache</th><th>After: MethodCache</th></tr>
<tr><td>

```cs
public async Task<User> GetUserAsync(int id)
{
    var key = $"user:{id}";
    if (_cache.TryGetValue(key, out User? user))
        return user!;

    // Two callers can both miss and both hit the database
    user = await _db.LoadUserAsync(id);
    _cache.Set(key, user, TimeSpan.FromMinutes(10));
    return user;
}

public async Task RenameAsync(int id, string name)
{
    await _db.RenameAsync(id, name);
    _cache.Remove($"user:{id}");
    // ...and every other key that held this user
}
```

</td><td>

```cs
[Cache(Duration = "00:10:00", Tags = ["user:{id}"])]
Task<User> GetUserAsync(int id);

[CacheInvalidate(Tags = ["user:{id}"])]
Task RenameAsync(int id, string name);
```

</td></tr>
</table>

## Steps

1. Add the `MethodCache` package and call `builder.Services.AddMethodCache()` after your registrations
   ([Getting started](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md)).
2. If the class has no interface, extract one. Callers must use the interface, because the cache is a decorator around
   it.
3. Move the caching settings to `[Cache]` on the interface method, and delete the cache code from the implementation.
4. Replace each `Remove(key)` with `[CacheInvalidate(Tags = ...)]` on the method that changes the data, and give the
   cached methods matching tags ([Invalidation](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/invalidation.md)).
5. Code that can't move to an attribute, such as a cached call in the middle of a method, uses
   `ICacheManager.GetOrCreateAsync` with the key it already has ([Manual caching](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/manual-caching.md)).

Migrate one service at a time; both caches can run side by side.

## What maps to what

| IMemoryCache | MethodCache |
|--------------|-------------|
| `TryGetValue` + `Set` | `[Cache]`, or `GetOrCreateAsync` with your key |
| `SetAbsoluteExpiration` | `Duration` |
| `SetSlidingExpiration` | `SlidingExpiration`, capped by `Duration` |
| `Remove(key)` | `[CacheInvalidate]` with tags, or `InvalidateKeysAsync` |
| `Size` and `SizeLimit` | `Weigher` and `WeightLimit` ([Memory cache](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/memory-cache.md)) |
| `Priority` | Not needed: W-TinyLFU keeps the entries that are read often |
| `GetOrCreateAsync`, which may run the factory several times at once | Concurrent misses share one call |
| A separate `IDistributedCache` | `AddMethodCache(mc => mc.UseRedis(...))`, with the memory cache kept in sync ([Distributed cache](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/distributed-cache.md)) |

## Differences to know

- **Keys are generated** from the method and its arguments ([Cache keys](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/keys.md)). Check that every argument
  that changes the result is a parameter, not a field of the class.
- **`null` is cached** by default. Set `MethodCacheMemoryOptions.CacheNullValues = false` ([Memory cache](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/memory-cache.md#null-values)) if your old code skipped `null`.
- **Exceptions are never cached**, as before.


---

<!-- source: src/MethodCache.Redis/README.md -->

# MethodCache.Redis

Redis as MethodCache's distributed cache. Results are shared between application instances, and invalidations reach
every instance's in-memory cache over Redis pub/sub.

Install it at the same version as `MethodCache`.

## Usage

```cs
builder.Services.AddMethodCache(mc => mc.UseRedis("localhost:6379"));
```

With options:

```cs
builder.Services.AddMethodCache(mc => mc
    .UseRedis(options => options.Configuration = "redis1:6379,redis2:6379,password=...")
    .Distributed(options => options.KeyPrefix = "orders-api:"));   // data and backplane use the same final prefix
```

To share a connection your app already has instead:

```cs
builder.Services.AddMethodCache(mc => mc.UseRedis(options =>
    options.ConnectionMultiplexerFactory = sp => sp.GetRequiredService<IConnectionMultiplexer>()));
```

- Set `Configuration` or `ConnectionMultiplexerFactory`. Startup fails when neither is set, so a missing configuration
  section never makes MethodCache connect to `localhost`.
- MethodCache keeps its own cache and connection, so your app's `IDistributedCache` and Redis settings are left alone.
- The connection opens on first use, on the thread pool, so the application starts while Redis is down and a slow
  connect never holds up a call.
- MethodCache doesn't dispose a shared connection. Disposing the service provider removes MethodCache's own
  subscriptions.

## How it works

- MethodCache reads Redis on an in-memory miss and writes new results to both.
- Invalidating a tag stores the time of the invalidation, and entries with that tag written before it are treated as
  missing, so no tag sets are kept in Redis. An older invalidation that arrives late never undoes a newer one.
- Every invalidation is also published on the `<prefix>invalidations` channel, so every instance drops its in-memory
  copies at once.
- Pub/sub delivers nothing while a connection is down. When the instance is subscribed again, it clears its in-memory
  cache. Reconnecting retries after 1 second, then twice as long each time, up to 30 seconds.

## Memory and eviction

Invalidations are stored as keys beside the entries. If Redis evicts one under memory pressure, the entries it
invalidated are served again until they expire. Set `maxmemory-policy noeviction` on the Redis MethodCache uses (or give
it a Redis of its own) and give it enough memory. The `volatile-*` policies, the default of some managed Redis
services, can evict them too. A full Redis with `noeviction` refuses writes, which MethodCache handles like an outage.
See
[Keep invalidations from being evicted](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/distributed-cache.md#keep-invalidations-from-being-evicted).

## When Redis is down

MethodCache keeps answering from memory and your methods; Redis never fails or stalls a call. Each call is capped at
`OperationTimeout` (1 second), Redis is skipped for `CircuitBreakerDuration` (10 seconds) after a failure, and
invalidations are queued and retried instead of throwing. The first failure and the recovery are logged.

The [distributed cache guide](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/distributed-cache.md)
covers outages, consistency between instances, serialization and the `DistributedCacheOptions` that tune all of this.
The exact behavior is in the
[distributed cache reference](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/reference/distributed.md).

## Options

| Option | Default | Description |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| `Configuration` | none | StackExchange.Redis configuration string |
| `ConnectionMultiplexerFactory` | none | Returns an existing connection to share instead of opening one |
| `EnableBackplane` | `true` | Send invalidations to other instances over pub/sub |

`DistributedCacheOptions.KeyPrefix` applies to values, invalidations and the channel. The first instance that uses a
prefix fixes its minimum `TagRetention`; a shorter setting fails at startup, so use a new prefix to lower it.


---

<!-- source: src/MethodCache.SqlServer/README.md -->

# MethodCache.SqlServer

SQL Server as MethodCache's distributed cache. Results are shared between application instances, and invalidations reach every instance's in-memory cache through a table that each instance polls.

Install it at the same version as `MethodCache`.

## Why this package

- **One shared cache for every instance.** Results live in each instance's memory and in SQL Server, so a result one instance computed is a hit for the others, and survives restarts.
- **Invalidation reaches every instance.** Invalidating a key or tag removes it from SQL Server, and every other instance drops its in-memory copy on its next poll (every second by default).
- **Tags work across instances**, without tag tables: invalidating a tag stores when it happened, stored atomically so a late, older invalidation never undoes a newer one.
- **No new infrastructure.** If you already run SQL Server, the schema and tables are created when the application starts.
- **SQL Server never breaks your app.** Calls are capped at one second, a circuit breaker skips SQL Server while it is down, and invalidations are queued until it is back.

Microsoft's `AddDistributedSqlServerCache()` (`SqlServerCache`) can't be used for this: it has no atomic invalidation timestamps, so MethodCache rejects it at startup, and it has no way to tell other instances to drop their in-memory copies. This package uses the same table layout, adds both, and keeps its own cache instance so your app's `IDistributedCache` is left alone.

## SQL Server or Redis?

| | SQL Server | Redis |
|---|---|---|
| Infrastructure | The SQL Server you already have | A Redis server |
| Other instances drop their in-memory copy | On their next poll (every second by default) | At once (pub/sub) |
| Load when idle | Every instance polls the invalidations table | None |
| Each distributed cache read or write | A SQL Server query | A Redis command |

Choose SQL Server when you already run it and a delay of about a second before other instances see an invalidation is fine; choose [Redis](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/src/MethodCache.Redis/README.md) when invalidations must reach other instances at once, or many instances would poll the database.

Only Microsoft SQL Server is supported: the package uses T-SQL locking hints and `Microsoft.Data.SqlClient`. For PostgreSQL, use [MethodCache.PostgreSql](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/src/MethodCache.PostgreSql/README.md), whose backplane also reaches other instances at once; MySQL and other databases are not supported.

## Usage

```cs
builder.Services.AddMethodCache(mc => mc.UseSqlServer(builder.Configuration.GetConnectionString("Cache")!));
```

With options:

```cs
builder.Services.AddMethodCache(mc => mc.UseSqlServer(options =>
{
    options.ConnectionString = connectionString;
    options.SchemaName = "cache";
    options.BackplanePollingInterval = TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(500);
}));
```

## Tables

By default the schema and three tables are created when the application starts, if they do not exist. Startup waits at most three seconds for that; if SQL Server is down, creation is retried in the background and methods run uncached until it succeeds.

- `MethodCache` holds the entries, in the layout `Microsoft.Extensions.Caching.SqlServer` uses (the same as `dotnet sql-cache create`).
- `MethodCacheSchema` contains the schema version (currently 1). Existing unversioned or unknown schemas are rejected.
- `MethodCacheInvalidations` holds recent invalidations for the backplane. Applications that share it are kept
  apart by `KeyPrefix` (compared exactly, whatever the SQL collation).

If the application's login may not create tables, set `CreateTablesIfMissing = false` and create them in a migration instead.

### Required backplane schema

The invalidations table needs a `Scope binary(32) NOT NULL` column and the indexes `Index_Scope_Id (Scope, Id)` and
`Index_Scope_CreatedAt (Scope, CreatedAt)`. MethodCache refuses a table without them instead of changing it, and logs
the error; an error found during the startup wait also fails startup. With `CreateTablesIfMissing = false`, create the
current schema yourself.

## When SQL Server is down

MethodCache keeps answering from memory and your methods; SQL Server never fails or stalls a call.

- Every SQL Server call is capped at `OperationTimeout` (1 second).
- After a failure or timeout, MethodCache skips SQL Server for `CircuitBreakerDuration` (10 seconds), then one call checks whether it is back. The first failure and the recovery are logged.
- Invalidations that SQL Server doesn't accept are queued and retried until it does. They never throw. Until they are stored, this instance doesn't read entries from SQL Server, so an invalidated value can't come back.
- A value set directly while SQL Server is down stays in this instance's memory; the value it replaced is removed from SQL Server and the other instances once SQL Server is back.
- `ClockSkewTolerance` (2 seconds) covers servers whose clocks differ: a tag invalidation also applies to entries created up to that long after it.

```cs
builder.Services.AddMethodCache(mc => mc.Distributed(options =>
{
    options.OperationTimeout = TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(500);
    options.CircuitBreakerDuration = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30);
}));
```

## Options

| Option | Default | Description |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| `ConnectionString` | (required) | SQL Server connection string |
| `SchemaName` | `dbo` | Schema of the cache, invalidations and schema-version tables |
| `TableName` | `MethodCache` | Table for cache entries |
| `InvalidationsTableName` | `MethodCacheInvalidations` | Table the backplane uses |
| `ConnectionStringFactory` | none | Resolves a connection string once from DI at binding |
| `CreateTablesIfMissing` | `true` | Create the schema and tables at startup |
| `EnableBackplane` | `true` | Share invalidations with other instances |
| `BackplanePollingInterval` | 1 second | How often each instance reads new invalidations |
| `BackplaneRetention` | 1 hour | How long invalidations are kept; at least one minute. Instances that share a `KeyPrefix` keep them as long as the longest retention any of them has used |

## How it works

- Cache commands never join your `TransactionScope`: MethodCache sets `Enlist=false` on its connection string, so a
  scope that rolls back doesn't undo cache writes or invalidations, and never becomes a distributed transaction.
- MethodCache reads SQL Server on an in-memory miss and writes new results to both.
- Expired rows are removed by one `DELETE` every 5 minutes on each instance. With a very large table, keep an index on
  `ExpiresAtTime` (`dotnet sql-cache create` and `CreateTablesIfMissing` add one).
- Values are JSON by default. A method whose results don't read back unchanged stays in memory only, with one warning
  ([Serialization](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/distributed-cache.md#serialization)).
  For MessagePack, add `MethodCache.Serialization.MessagePack` and call `UseMessagePack()`.
- Keys are stored as a SHA-256 hash of the exact key, so keys that SQL collation would treat as equal (casing,
  trailing spaces) stay distinct, and keys of any length fit.
- Invalidating a tag stores the time of the invalidation, and entries with that tag written before it are treated as
  missing, so no tag tables are needed. An older invalidation that arrives late never undoes a newer one.
- Every invalidation also adds a row to the invalidations table. Other instances read new rows every
  `BackplanePollingInterval` and drop their in-memory copies. A long-running transaction elsewhere never holds back
  newer invalidations.
- An instance that couldn't read the invalidations table for half of `BackplaneRetention` may have missed
  invalidations, so it clears its in-memory cache.
